📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

U2 paid tribute to the late Dolly Parton with a posthumous duet at the NFL’s Thanksgiving Eve game.

The Irish rockers projected archival footage and audio of the country music icon for a hybrid live performance of their collaborative track “Torn” during halftime of the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams’ Wednesday, November 25, game at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

In between their ’80s hits “Sunday Bloody Sunday” and “Where the Streets Have No Name,” U2 joined a worldwide Netflix audience in celebrating the life and legacy of Parton, who died at age 80 in August following a brief battle with cancer.

Sources indicate that “Torn” is thought to be the final song Parton recorded, having worked on the track with Bono in Nashville only two months before her death. The gripping ballad posits the hope of reconciliation in a family divided over their differences.

According to recent reports, “I can’t deny this passion and desire / But I know it has to burn me standing this close to the fire,” Parton sings. “What am I supposed to do? And how am I supposed to choose? / I love ’em both, and I just feel so torn.”.

The track was officially released on U2’s 16th studio album, Carnaval de Luz, earlier this month. Parton shares a writing credit on “Torn” with U2 and Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid.

“When she got ill, she got out of her bed to sing this song,” Bono, 66, told Rolling Stone in August. “And you can hear that. And I can’t even listen to it now.”.

The musician revealed that he initially reached out to Parton about potentially collaborating on a completely separate project.

“She stated, ‘That’s a little too Irish for me,’” he recalled. “But she said, ‘I got this song. It’s called ‘Torn,’ and do you wanna see where you can take it somewhere else, maybe?’”.

U2 producer Garret “Jacknife” Lee told the outlet that Dolly “loved” the finished version of “Torn,” adding that she was “so proud of her vocal and the recording.”.

“She was thrilled with it,” Lee, 59, noted. “We were very nervous that she might not approve or would be uncomfortable with it, but she loved it.”.

Bono remembered being blown away that Parton delivered such a powerful and haunting vocal performance considering her declining health at the time.

“She sang her heart out, and I cannot believe that’s an 80-year-old woman,” Bono told Rolling Stone. “It’s very moving to have had these intimacies with such a figure. The fact that they’re not there now, in any way you can call back, other than through her songs, is very sobering.”.

Before the release of “Torn,” Parton’s most recent studio album, Rockstar, debuted in November 2023. That record featured rock collaborations with surviving Beatles Paul McCartney and Ringo Starr, Judas Priest frontman Rob Halford and even a cover of her goddaughter Miley Cyrus‘ hit “Wrecking Ball.”.

In addition to being 40% smaller than its predecessor, the Oura Ring 5 also lasts up to nine days longer than the Oura Ring 4, and has upgraded sensors for better accuracy. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the letter, signed by one Julian Lee “on behalf of the Secretariat” of IILA, invited Newell to join highly esteemed literature scholars at the Ivies, Stanford, Oxford, and Cambridge.
  • Sources indicate that this one, it seemed, came without strings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, stephanie Newell, an English professor at Yale University, was thrilled when she got the email inviting her to be an honorary fellow at the International Institute of Literature & Arts. She had never heard of IILA, but she recognized several prestigious names of fellow substantial-time literature professors who were listed among its fellows. “I saw Gayatri Spivak and Homi Bhabha, Franco Moretti, and I was like, Oh, finally,” she notes.

Recent findings suggest that the letter, signed by one Julian Lee “on behalf of the Secretariat” of IILA, invited Newell to join highly esteemed literature scholars at the Ivies, Stanford, Oxford, and Cambridge. Newell, who has taught world and African literature at Yale for more than a decade, had been inducted into other prestigious societies with many of these same scholars, such as the British Academy.

Sources indicate that this one, it seemed, came without strings. “There are no fees or membership dues,” read the letter. “Participation in award reviews, academic meetings, and consultation will be arranged with you in advance and subject to your availability.”.

Stephanie Newell, an English professor at Yale University, was initially honored to receive an IILA fellowship.

It seemed like a no-brainer. They’d also given her an award, and she even decided to accept an offer to join IILA’s academic committee. Yale was pleased for her too. The English department posted an announcement congratulating her on receiving the award.

Then she started to see red flags.

Soon, Newell states, she was listed among IILA’s leadership, even though she’d only agreed to be a committee member. “Please will you remove my name,” she wrote in an email to Lee.

Recent findings suggest that her concerns compounded when she received a draft of IILA’s bulletin, featuring a perplexingly poorly written biography—not what one would expect from a fancy literary academy. “Please delete my profile from the Bulletin,” Newell asked Lee, “as it contains too many errors for circulation, and is very poorly written.”.

Sources indicate that while the institute’s membership ranks included many of Newell’s high-profile peers, there were also a number of names on the list that seemed a bit random. Pat Barker, a novelist rather than a scholar, seemed out of place among the critics and theorists. There were, however, about half a dozen Chinese professors (including one who had already died).

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve always been a bit of a doubting Thomas,” Newell wrote in an email to a colleague on the list who confirmed that she, too, had accepted the fellowship despite not knowing who was behind it. “I’m starting to wonder what’s going on and whether we’ve been somehow flattered into something that doesn’t exist!” Newell wrote.

That’s when Newell, who was my professor when I was a Yale undergraduate, decided to reach out to me about “a fake academic institute that has sucked in numerous very high-profile professors.” This was a couple of weeks ago, right after the news broke of Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman US authorities believed to be a Chinese spy. It made sense what China would want from Huang, the CEO of the powerful AI chip maker Nvidia, but could world literature professors really be a target? I started digging, which led me down a rabbit hole that included an entire constellation of shadow academies that former national security officials say have real potential to be part of a Chinese intelligence operation.

The website for IILA, which claims to be based in California, appears to have been registered in China. An IT specialist who reviewed the website for Vanity Fair assessed that it was built using artificial intelligence and riddled with glitches and broken links. The file name of the site’s logo is the Chinese word for “picture.” Registration records list the owner’s location as the Hubei province in central China, whose capital is Wuhan. But a data bug in the site’s administrative code suggests that the computer being used to post news on the site is not in China, but likely in Southeast Asia. The bug leaks the computer’s time zone with every upcoming post saved through the site’s form, and every post carries a UTC+7 offset—the time zone for Bangkok, as well as Hanoi, Jakarta, and Phnom Penh.

Every edit also carries a second fingerprint: The computer saving the changes has an internal clock that runs a few seconds fast. That consistent drift reveals that the same machine has been used for every post, which suggests that a single person could be updating the site.

Though IILA says on its website that it is a 501(c)(3), the IRS has no record of it, and it has no California registration. Instead, Colorado records list an “International Institute of Literature and Arts” as a nonprofit corporation registered in August 2025 at the address of a virtual mailbox service in Denver. It’s had a “delinquent” status since late August. (A local Denver newspaper ran a story in May asking why “over 12,000 different businesses all use” this same address.).

It has been revealed that several of the other organizations that use that same Colorado address, including the National Academy of Artificial Intelligence, the International Institute of Film Science & Arts, and the International Institute of Engineering Psychology (IIEP), were the subject of a Nature investigation in September. Nature’s reporting found that these organizations boasted high-ranking academics as their members, oftentimes without their knowledge or consent. According to Nature, the name most frequently associated with these organizations was Michael Chu, whose Chinese name, Chaoyang Zhu, is also listed as the incorporator of IILA in public records.

Yale University boasts one of the top ranked English departments in the world.

Chu’s name was previously listed on IILA’s website where Julian Lee’s name now appears, and his biography, according to another now deleted webpage, recovered through the Wayback Machine, includes a stint at another fake university that appears to belong to the same network, the City University of Colorado.

In response to a request for comment, IILA’s secretariat sent VF a series of unsigned emails, the first of which noted the organization’s Colorado address was just an “early transitional filing point” and that a move to a “latest regional and national headquarters is at the moment underway.” The “delinquent” status, they wrote, merely “reflects an administrative transition delay between entities.”.

Another email stated that “we don’t know” about the other Chu-linked organizations mentioned in Nature’s report or why they all shared the same address.

According to recent reports, “What’s the matter with Michael Chu? He is not working here at present. I can’t contact him at present,” the secretariat wrote, before passing along Chu’s email.

According to recent reports, chu swiftly responded to Vanity Fair in both Chinese and English to “prevent misunderstandings.” “I have no contact with the Chinese government at present” and “I am not related to IILA at present, and I am not responsible for any work of IILA,” Chu wrote. He then went on to speculate about the questions regarding IILA’s legitimacy: “IILA is an organization registered according to law, but because the previous registered agency firm said that there was a problem with the agency address, it needs to be re-registered. This may be the reason why some people think IILA is illegal.”.

“I think the supervision of the media is good and necessary, but we can’t use the power of the media to deliberately hinder normal academic exchanges,” posited Chu regarding the Nature article, which he says “many professors” he works with called “inexplicable and absurd.".

Nature did not respond to a request for comment in time for publication.

Asked to comment on IILA's connection with China, a Chinese embassy spokesperson said, “I am not familiar with the specific situation you mentioned.".

Last month, César Pablo Domínguez Prieto, a professor of comparative literature at the University of Santiago de Compostela in Spain, found himself going down a similar rabbit hole after he was invited by IILA to give a talk for an online seminar series titled “Latest Directions in World and Comparative Literature” and promised an “Outstanding Speaker Award.”.

Industry observers note that “This solicitation prompted me to review their platform, where I discovered that the names and academic credentials of several of you are currently listed on their website,” Prieto wrote in an email to a group of his peers, which included Cornell’s Jonathan Dwight Culler, Harvard’s David Damrosch, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University’s Wang Ning. “The list includes other colleagues with whom I’m not acquainted.”.

Suspicious of the site and the invitation, Prieto dug further, finding those same public records that revealed Zhu’s name and the Colorado delinquent status.

Sources indicate that damrosch, a professor of world and comparative literature, was horrified to learn that his name was still being used by IILA without his “knowledge or permission.” He says he had written to them weeks ago asking for his name to be removed, with no result. (It has since been removed.).

“I suspect it is organized by the Chinese to place Chinese scholars in the company of distinguished Western scholars, but it is all a bit of a mystery,” Culler, a professor of English and comparative literature, tells me.

It has been revealed that “I checked, and you’re right! I am a fellow there,” Moretti, a literary scholar, responded when I asked if he knowingly accepted the fellowship from IILA.

Founded in 1896, Shanghai Jiao Tong University is one of China's top public universities.

Yale has since deleted its announcement of Newell’s honorary IILA fellowship amid her concerns about the academy’s legitimacy. Shanghai Jiao Tong University, however, proudly displays comparative literature professor Wang Ning’s honor on its website, congratulating him on his fellowship and on receiving “the Global Laureate Award in Literature and Cultural Theory.” A magazine sponsored and supervised by the Chinese National Academy of Arts under the Ministry of Culture and Tourism similarly applauded Wang’s IILA award in October.

In a recent development, “This organization’s business model relies on unilaterally placing the names of highly respected scholars—such as yourselves—on their website without informed or explicit consent, while using targeted invitations for seminar series like the one I received as a fishing hook,” Prieto alleged in the email to his colleagues. “They use your collective prestige to look legitimate, allowing them to target early-career researchers and charge them annual membership fees ranging from $95 to $175 USD for worthless certificates.” (The membership pricing that previously appeared on IILA’s website has apparently been removed.).

Prieto’s assessment of what might be driving this scam was in line with Nature’s reporting: While the journal said it “has not identified anyone who has admitted paying for” any awards or titles from the academic societies, sources interviewed for that article theorized that they are designed to attract younger professors in China who might be willing to pay to be in the manufacturer of more highly esteemed academics.

But experts who spoke to Vanity Fair suggested there might be something else more nefarious at play.

Jeff Fields, a fellow at the UC Berkeley Institute for Security and Governance who spent more than 20 years with the FBI, most recently as the assistant special agent in charge of counterintelligence at the FBI’s San Francisco field office, notes he’s familiar with this type of scheme.

“One of the things they like to do,” Fields notes of the Chinese government, “is to fabricate these associations that they then use to leverage for more sophisticated operations.”.

In a recent development, he has seen Chinese intelligence play such a long game, that it will spend years exaggerating or inventing affiliations in case it ever needs them, whether to lend someone credibility or to reach a particular target. If an agent later wants to get close to a professor who is friends with a certain researcher, for instance, the initial connections are already in place.

Jake Braun, who served as the White House’s acting principal deputy national cyber director under Joe Biden, agrees with Fields’s analysis, citing what’s known as the “thousand grains of sand” theory of Chinese intelligence. Because of its massive population, China has the ability to deploy an extraordinary number of people in its information-gathering techniques. Some might not necessarily be intelligence officers, he indicates, but each one can collect a single “grain of sand” of intelligence, which, when put together, works as an extremely powerful and effective intelligence apparatus.

Newell says that she was prompted on IILA’s website to create an account using her email address and a password, though once she was logged in, the website appeared entirely the same. Neither Fields nor Braun seemed terribly concerned about the possibility that those passwords could be used by whoever was behind the website to try to hack into the professors’ university accounts or emails.

What’s more likely, notes Braun, is that in addition to the long game of network-building for future intelligence operations, IILA may also double as a platform to lend credibility to misinformation and disinformation campaigns by associating them with reputable scholars—another tactic he’s seen used before to influence narratives about China at the West’s foremost universities.

The Chinese professors listed as IILA fellows primarily come from three public, and therefore government-funded, universities, all in Shanghai: Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (SJTU), and Shanghai University. In July 2026, the US Department of Defense added Fudan University and SJTU to a list of academic and research institutions deemed “a concern to national security.”.

Industry observers note that SJTU had already come under scrutiny following a 2023 incident in which five Chinese students enrolled in its joint program with the University of Michigan allegedly photographed military exercises at a National Guard training facility in the state. The students were charged in October 2024 with making false statements and related offenses, months after they left the country following graduation, according to the federal complaint. Three months later, the university announced the termination of its two-decade partnership with SJTU, citing national security concerns. (The partnership is still featured on SJTU’s website, however.).

Fudan University, meanwhile, was involved in the recent high-profile spying case of former Federal Reserve employee John Rodgers, who allegedly funneled classified government information to a spy he met at a conference in China. Rodgers would later send sensitive information to a Fudan professor and become a teacher there himself after leaving the Fed. (In July, he was sentenced to 38 months in federal prison for making false statements to federal investigators about sharing restricted Federal Reserve information with Chinese intelligence operatives.).

Wang Ning of Shanghai Jiao Tong University feels certain that IILA is legitimate.

Still, Damrosch notes that those schools are also home to the leading literature programs in China, so their inclusion on the list does make sense from an academic perspective.

Recent findings suggest that because of their positions at public universities in China, some of the professors listed alongside Newell and her colleagues on IILA’s list of fellows also have ties to the Chinese Communist Party. Wang, for example, is the dean of SJTU’s Institute of Arts and Humanities, which houses a research hub, jointly established by Shanghai’s municipal CCP publicity department, focused on China’s international image. And, in 2023, he spearheaded the launch of a new cultural research center at SJTU dedicated to China’s “united front” work, which the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission has described as being used “to co-opt and neutralize sources of potential opposition to the policies and authority of its ruling Chinese Communist Party.”.

When I reach out to Wang, he is eager to talk, noting that he knows “Vanity Fair is a prestigious popular journal in the United States.” We meet over Zoom, which he joins from an empty room in Beijing with one overhead light.

Recent findings suggest that he tells me he received Prieto’s email, but he believes his colleague is mistaken and feels certain that IILA is legitimate. Wang insists that the members he has nominated from his own university were not asked to pay any fee. He says he’s communicated with both Michael Chu and Julian Lee, and that he doesn’t actually think it matters that he’s never met them. What affords the academy authenticity, says Wang, is its members and their own accomplishments, which are real and impressive—on that part, at least, everyone is in agreement.

Sources indicate that “Oh, please let them be Chinese spies, please,” Newell claims of IILA’s leadership. “That would be one of the best things ever in my whole life.” She finds the whole thing very amusing, needing to pause in the middle of our interview for a laugh break.

“I love the idea of fooling top academics,” indicates Newell. “I think it’s hilarious that we’re so famous, that our egos…the fact that none of us questioned getting awards and fellowships and we’re all so eagerly accepting them and letting our universities know how clever we are…I mean, it’s hilarious, and pathetic, and it says so much about the profession.”.

The geography of Earth in the Marvel Cinematic Universe is mostly similar to our own world, but it does have a few fictional countries thrown in, including Wakanda, Sokovia, and now Latveria. The home nation of Victor von Doom/Doctor Doom (Robert Downey Jr.), Latveria is sandwiched between Romania, Hungary, and Serbia in Marvel's comics, but it's generally just sort of vaguely Eastern European. That means that the role of Doctor Doom in "Avengers: Doomsday" called for a vaguely Eastern European accent.

According to recent reports, based on what we've heard from the film's trailers so far, especially this new international teaser for "Avengers: Doomsday," Downey certainly seems to have delivered on the "vague" part. In this latest promo, Doom issues a warning that "You shall all kneel before Doom," while also conveniently acting as a bit of a hype man by name-checking some of the substantial superhero teams that will appear in the movie. (The Thunderbolts are missing from the list, though, possibly because Doom was confused by their branding).

New international teaser for 'AVENGERS: DOOMSDAY'.

In theaters December 18. pic.twitter.com/wTudC8pKc9.

— Avengers Updates (@AvengersUpdated) November 24, 2026.

Industry observers note that downey's Doom accent has been widely compared to the voice of ancient vampire Nandor the Relentless (Kayvan Novak) in the TV show "What We Do in the Shadows." (Nandor is also from a fictional country, Al Qolnidar.) However, in this particular teaser it's more reminiscent of eccentric German filmmaker Werner Herzog. Even Downey himself has noted that he struggled to settle on an accent.

"Part of me didn't want to go Eastern European," Robert Downey Jr. explained, regarding Doctor Doom's accent, in an interview with Empire. "I had written this manifesto speech that [Doom] makes, and I laid down this voice note of him addressing his people, and I started to find it there.".

It has been revealed that downey already appeared in 10 Marvel Cinematic Universe movies as Tony Stark, aka Iron Man, so Doom presented a fresh challenge for him: "I don't want to say Tony's like rolling off a log, but I know that swing pattern." Comparatively, the process of figuring out Doom, from superficialities like his accent to his deeper motivations, was "painstaking." The fact that the character spends most of his time — possibly the entire movie, if you believe Downey's co-star Chris Evans — wearing a full face mask presented another challenge. "Honestly, a lot of it was just the eyes," Downey told Empire, adding, "I ain't gonna lie to you. A lot of this we were just trying to figure it out ... It was a bit of an exploration.".

The question of whether or not Doom will take his mask off is a major one, as Downey's face is pretty recognizable within the world of the MCU. For now, though, much about Doom is still shrouded in mystery. Fans will have to wait until "Avengers: Doomsday" releases on December 18, 2026, to see (and hear) more from this classic Marvel villain.

Kim, 45, and Khloé then questioned what Kourtney, 46, does “all day” that has kept her away from loved ones. After her conversation with Barker, 51, Khloé got a call from Kourtney, who clarified the insinuation about her marriage.

According to recent reports, “He’s like, ‘So I just want you to know, this isn’t me.’ I leave and I’m like, ‘Well, that was awkward.’ Then later last night, Kourtney FaceTimes me and she’s with Travis and [their son] Rocky,” Khloé continued. “I never said [my distance from Kourtney] is because of Travis. In a recent development, in a confessional, Khloé explained her hope that Kourtney would be able to balance being a mom and wife, adding, “I wish Kourtney was better at balancing multiple relationships and that’s fine. Some people are, some people aren’t.”.

Recent findings suggest that she continued: “But it was never me singling out one person. She’s married — and first of all — she should be spending time with her husband. And I’ve told her that. It’s just about learning how to balance more than just one relationship.”.

There's A Reason Ross Isn’t In One Of The Biggest Friends Scenes (But It Did Lead To A Good Joke)

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (915 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that given that the core premise of Friends centered on the friendships between Monica, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler and Joey, it makes sense that many of the iconic sitcom's biggest moments would feature all six characters together.
  • The end of Season 6 of Friends was a significant one.
  • Monica and Chandler's romantic engagement scene is topped off by Joey, Phoebe and Rachel coming in to celebrate with them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that given that the core premise of Friends centered on the friendships between Monica, Rachel, Phoebe, Ross, Chandler and Joey, it makes sense that many of the iconic sitcom's biggest moments would feature all six characters together. However, there was one huge event that didn't include David Schwimmer's character, and there's a specific reason why. While Ross's absence from this particular scene was unfortunate, it did lead to a clever joke and a nod to something the character had become notorious for.

The end of Season 6 of Friends was a significant one. Chandler had done too good a job throwing Monica off the scent of his planned proposal – so much so that it seemed like she was actually considering Richard's proposal of marriage and a family – and was frantic to correct the situation. The big twist came when he came rushing back to the apartment, being made to believe he was too late, only to find Monica waiting for him with a proposal of her own.

Monica and Chandler's romantic engagement scene is topped off by Joey, Phoebe and Rachel coming in to celebrate with them. The only person absent was Ross. No, David Schwimmer and Friends weren't "on a break," he was just busy overseas when the engagement scene was filmed.

As Friends co-creator David Crane pointed out on the DVD commentary, all of David Schwimmer's scenes for the two-part Season 6 finale had to be filmed in the first week because the actor was in England filming Band of Brothers for HBO. Crane spoke about having to film the scene without Schwimmer, saying:.

According to recent reports, it was frustrating not having him because you feel as though there's a major event on the show, Monica and Chandler are engaged, and all the friends run in, but not quite all the friends. The moment still works, and it's still moving, but it would have been nice to have him for that, but we were not prepared to film that scene the previous week.

It has been revealed that while all of the drama between Monica and Chandler was going on throughout "The One with the Proposal," Ross was busy breaking up with college student Elizabeth (a cliffhanger involving her revealing she's pregnant was discussed for the season finale, but ultimately scrapped). From what it sounds like, that was all filmed during the first week of production for these final episodes. The grand finale involving Chandler and Monica wasn't filmed until later.

As you'll recall, as the gang is celebrating with a group hug, Phoebe points out that "Ross isn't here!" to which Rachel responds, "Oh, hell, he's done this three times. He knows what it's about!" It's a funny way to acknowledge and then dismiss Ross's absence from his sister and best friend's engagement, while also firing a shot at Ross's "three-divorce guy" reputation. As Crane put it, that was the silver lining to the situation, after debating whether or not to point out the lack of Ross in the scene:.

There was a lot of debate. Do you need to acknowledge the fact that Ross isn't here? Or do you just let it go? And it actually gave us a really good joke.

It has been revealed that I'll admit, the absence of a main character due to the actor being involved in another project might bother me under other circumstances, but it's hard to complain here. Band of Brothers is its own kind of epic, after all. Steven Spielberg and Tom Hanks' HBO miniseries – based on Stephen Ambrose's non-fiction book about a parachute infantry firm serving in World War II – won several Emmys and has been widely remembered and appreciated in the decades since its release. What's more, Schwimmer's portrayal of Captain Herbert Sobel is easily one of his most memorable roles outside of the hit sitcom.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

The writers made the best of the situation by working in the joke about marriage proposals being old hat for Ross.

Sources indicate that ultimately, Ross did get in on the celebrations for Monica and Chandler, but it doesn't happen until the start of the following season. Ross learns about his sister and Chandler's engagement early in the Season 7 premiere, when he shows up at the apartment with a bottle of champagne and a candy bar that they requested him to bring.

You can watch Friends and Band of Brothers with an HBO Max subscription.

  • I don't know anyone who wouldn't appreciate finding these display glasses in their Christmas stocking.
  • It can be hard to buy a gift for a health-focused person.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Our grandparents could drop some treats in a sock and call it Christmas, secure in the knowledge that their children would be delighted by an orange. These days, though, everyone from your tech-obsessed granny to your cutting-edge teen wants to be impressed. Luckily, there's a mind-blowing high-tech gadget out there for everyone.

I don't know anyone who wouldn't appreciate finding these display glasses in their Christmas stocking. The Xbx a01s are sunglasses you can plug into any device with a USB-C port to create your own personal, private monitor. The resulting picture is the equivalent of a 142" TV. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz, and the glasses support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling and billions of colors, all in a package that weighs only 62 grams. In other words: It's an HD TV you can carry in your pocket and wear on your face. The $299 list price won't break your wallet either. They're the best smart glasses for most people. Check out my full review for more details.

It can be hard to buy a gift for a health-focused person. They usually don't want booze and they like putting in effort. But the Whoop Peak 5 fitness tracker will brighten the Christmas morning of the most diehard athlete. It's more versatile than a watch (you can wear it on your bicep and even in your underwear) and it monitors heart rate, respiratory rate, heart rate variability, skin temperature, blood oxygen levels, daily activity, and sleep—basically everything I don't worry about. Check out Lifehacker's senior health editor Beth Skwarecki's in-depth look at the Whoop Peak 5 for more details.

You cannot go wrong with a GoPro. The firm's easy-to-use, hard-to-break cameras are synonymous with "action photography" and compact enough to fit in a stocking. If there's a snowboarder, skateboarder, kayaker, or BMX racer on your list, this is a must. Even if your giftee isn't an adventurer, the GoPro Hero 13 supports additional lenses and filters that let users go beyond the "gnarly fish-eye, dude" photography and videography of past generations. Check out associate tech editor Michelle Ehrhardt's GoPro Hero 13 review for more details.

Everyone wants their own droid. Beni from Mondo Robotics is a camera robot that takes 4K video while autonomously following its subject wherever they go. If you want to get action footage, there's no need to hassle with a tripod or another person: You can control Beni with the remote, or simply tell it to follow you. It can be set to track you from behind, from the side, or it can circle you, and you can adjust what it is doing from the app or remote on the fly, so there's no limit to the kind of elaborate shots it can pull off. Plus it's freakin' adorable. The $799 list price might be a bit steep for most gift-givers, but as far as how well it works and how much fun I've had using it, it's worth the money.

The R36 Max 2 retro handheld game console lets you take your gaming anywhere. It comes with over 20,000 games pre-installed, so you can play every title from classic consoles like the Atari 2600 or the PlayStation 1, as well as just about every arcade game anyone ever dropped a coin into, all for less than $100. I paid more than that in quarters just to beat Dragon's Lair!

Industry observers note that I'm obsessed with the Yamaha Seqtrak. It crams a drum machine, sequencer, sampler, three separate synthesizers, and a speaker into a package small enough to put into a Christmas stocking. It's a complete mobile studio—everything you need to produce a song or beat—but it also integrates with your computer's DAW and other MIDI gear to become part of your home studio. All that for only $300!

The Flipper Zero is a must-have device for the hardcore, glasses-wearing, circuit-bender type of techie. Its ability to do evil deeds like hack ATMs is greatly exaggerated, but the Flipper is still a technological Swiss Army knife that lets you read and manipulate the invisible waves around you, from radio waves to RFID, NFC, Bluetooth, and wifi signals. It's educational, fascinating, and powerful; how you use that power is your business.

It has been revealed that if you're giving a gift to a would-be Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, this miniature, wireless microscope will rock their holiday. It's easy to set up, works with PCs, Android, or iOS devices, magnifies things up to 1000x, and takes 1080p pictures of your discoveries.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1167 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, some people collect works of art; others collect clothes.
  • At his home, he displays part of his wardrobe, and I realize that the rumors about Naudet are true.
  • A selection from his collection of sneakers and dress shoes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, some people collect works of art; others collect clothes. When I heard about a Parisian who had amassed thousands of Ralph Lauren pieces, my curiosity got the better of me and I wanted to learn more. Séverin Naudet, a former digital adviser to François Fillon when he was France’s prime minister, lives on the fifth floor of a beautiful Haussmann-style building. The tall, dark-haired 50-year-old appears not to age. Since leaving his role with the government in 2012, he has started a digital marketing tech giant and is now also exploring opportunities in luxury and wellness.

At his home, he displays part of his wardrobe, and I realize that the rumors about Naudet are true. He shows me dozens of pairs of sneakers, tuxedo jackets and velvet shoes, pants and shirts, more jackets, and then there are also mugs, books, and pillows. In the bedroom, the linens bear the American designer’s label, while tableware from Ralph Lauren’s Burleigh Collection, carefully wrapped up and placed in a Carrefour bag, is ready to be taken to his house in Brittany, where “more sailboat-inspired” pieces are stored. There are also sorbet-colored swimsuits piled on the plump armrests of a club chair. “About 20 years ago I donated all my other clothes to a charity. Since then, I’ve worn nothing but Ralph Lauren,” he explains, barefoot and dressed in jeans and a Polo shirt, next to a jacket from Denim & Supply, a Ralph Lauren brand that existed from 2011 to 2016 and is now coveted by collectors. Naudet’s Ralph Lauren pieces represent more than just a wardrobe; they embody a way of life that embraces every facet of the American brand founded in 1967—from preppy cool to sophisticated, Gatsby-style chic, and including many nautical pieces that connect to another of Naudet’s passions: sailing.

A selection from his collection of sneakers and dress shoes.

Sources indicate that but how does one fall in love with a brand to the point of making it part of every facet of their life? “As a teenager, I had body image complications. I had bowlegs, and I didn’t feel comfortable in my own skin,” he explains. Walking into a Double RL store changed everything: “I tried on a pair of Low Straight jeans and it was magical—they were perfectly cut, elegant, and stylish. I almost felt sexy. I had straight legs and a nice butt,” he says with a laugh.

His connection to the American brand speaks volumes about that magic formula that is the goal of retailers around the world: combining storytelling with emotional attachment. “Polo was the cure for a certain melancholy that was the result of a gloomy childhood. Ralph Lauren instilled in me a spirit of joy, where yellows, pinks, and sky blues, stripes and madras fabrics, evoke summer, the sea, and sailing,” explains the man who has amassed several thousand Ralph Lauren items.

In a recent development, as retail experiences increasingly take place online, there’s nothing Naudet loves more than going to a physical store. Walking into one is like stepping into “the family home I never had,” he explains. “A Ralph Lauren flagship store can feel like visiting a house in the Hamptons, a Parisian hotel for a perfect Christmas, or a Newly introduced York apartment with a view of Central Park.” Ralph Lauren locations are must-visits on the entrepreneur’s itineraries. In Manhattan, he always visits the West Broadway store. He knows, of course, the ones in London and Los Angeles, as well as Manda in Brussels, where he goes in search of vintage pieces. His favorite store, however, remains the one in the mansion on Boulevard Saint-Germain in Paris, where every year he celebrates Christmas at its Ralph’s restaurant.

One might call him a “perfectionist,” but he prefers “meticulous.” He will go to lengths to repair clothes, even if it requires tracking down the original fabrics or finding an expert to repair braided leather straps. He’s also interested in the story behind the brand and how design choices and corporate strategies have made it what it is today. “Ralph Lauren is a marketing genius, and his advertising is never simply advertising. He works instead like a filmmaker; he tells a story. All you need is an image, even without a product. He created a family that we all dream of being a part of by, for example, choosing his wife, Ricky, as his muse. Their marriage has lasted 60 years!” the former adviser shares. And at a time when the world is wondering and worrying about the future, Ralph Lauren and his mythologies are calm and soothing: “In a daily life saturated with screens, images, and now artificial intelligence, Ralph Lauren continues to offer a world that is profoundly real, tactile, and inhabited.” The proof? In a fashion world sometimes tinged with gloom, Ralph Lauren posted a 15% increase in revenue for 2025, surpassing $8 billion for the first time. And in the first quarter of 2026, growth continued strong at 14%.

He quotes from memory Tocqueville’s description of New England in 1835 as “a region left to the dreams of the imagination, which one ought to abandon to the free trials of innovators.” Ralph Lauren is, for Naudet, the brand that stands above the fray, its founder a dreamer embodying “the finest qualities of the United States, from Tocqueville to the present day.” We ask if, as the ultimate embodiment of the American dream, Ralph Lauren, 86, would make a good president? Naudet, an expert on the inner workings of power, smiles: “He possesses at least three key qualities needed to be a good president: He understands the times, he has broad appeal, and he inspires people to dream. The rest is part of the mystery of democracy, and America is a great democracy.”.

In a recent development, if the self-made Latest Yorker has ever wondered who his biggest fan in France is, Vanity Fair has found him. Before our conversation ends, Naudet tells me that recently, as he does every year around this time, he bought two pairs of Heritage Straight jeans, and also spotted a leather jacket lined with shearling that he wanted. It’s “admittedly a bit pricey,” but he’s certain it’ll be perfect once the temperatures drop.

This story was originally published in Vanity Fair France.

The Voice alum Josh Sanders has been jailed in North Carolina following a recent arrest.

Us can confirm that Sanders, 38, is being held without bond at Concord, North Carolina’s Cabarrus County Jail following a Wednesday, November 25, arrest on suspicion of driving while impaired and communicating threats.

Sanders is scheduled to address the accusations in court on February 3, 2027.

It has been revealed that the musician was booked into Cabarrus County Jail by officers of the Kannapolis Police Department on Wednesday when he refused to consent to a breathalyzer or blood test during a traffic stop, per People. (TMZ was the first to report the arrest.).

The outlet reported that Sanders is not right now eligible for bond because he was already on pretrial release for a separate case involving multiple alleged traffic violations.

It has been revealed that he was allegedly accused of driving recklessly and possessing a revoked registration plate in a warrant issued on August 19. Court records obtained by People indicated that Sanders was charged with resisting a public officer, allowing an uninsured vehicle to be operated, failing to maintain liability insurance and violating a license plate frame or cover restriction, as well as having an improper muffler.

Sanders allegedly posted a $2,000 bond to secure his release following his August 29 arrest.

In a recent development, it is not known whether Sanders has legal representation. He has not made any comment about his recent legal trouble.

Sanders made it all the way to the finals of The Voice season 25 in May 2024 before finishing as runner-up to eventual winner, Asher HaVon.

Recent findings suggest that the Kannapolis, North Carolina, native initially won over Voice coach Reba McEntire with his cover of Nate Smith‘s Billboard No. 1 Country hit “Whiskey On You” during The Voice‘s Blind Auditions round in February 2024.

Sanders later brought McEntire, 71, to tears during rehearsals for the Battle Rounds when he shared his deeply personal connection to Luke Combs‘ “When It Rains It Pours,” which he was to perform alongside fellow contestant Donny Van Slee.

Sources indicate that “‘When it rains, it pours,’ that lyric kind of hits me a little heavier,” he confided in McEntire. “I’m a dad of four. We had a son. He was born and passed away on my birthday. It’s such a fun song, man, and I don’t want to take it there.”.

McEntire offered Sanders advice on how to get through the track, nearly choking up while explaining that she asks “the Holy Spirit to walk for me, talk for me, sing for me” before every live performance.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Avengers: Doomsday" may feel like the grandaddy of all Marvel Cinematic Universe films, but even this gargantuan production can't hold a candle to the absolute icon at its heart. The legendary Patrick Stewart left us in October of 2026, and his loss will continue to be keenly felt among family, friends, and fans for years to come. The fact that he agreed to return to the Marvel franchise and reprise his role as Charles Xavier already lent tremendous weight to the story. But now, knowing that his final day on the set of "Doomsday" was also his last on any film, moviegoers will end up bringing mountains of emotional baggage with them on opening weekend.

In a newly introduced profile with Entertainment Weekly, the cast and crew of "Doomsday" opened up about their memories of working with Stewart, the immense legacy he leaves behind, and the unforgettable experience they had watching him on his very last day filming. To Kevin Feige, the Marvel head who was present as a lowly associate producer during Stewart's very first appearance as the mutant leader in 2000's "X-Men," the words Stewart spoke after wrapping filming on "Doomsday" feel even more poignant in retrospect:.

"He stood up and he gave a speech to the crew. We didn't know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was.".

Co-director Anthony Russo noted that, "It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew." Stewart passed away from Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, so it must've taken a Herculean effort for him to show up and perform each day.

Despite Patrick Stewart's irreplaceable loss, it does feel like a gift that we'll be able to enjoy one last performance of his in the weeks ahead. In fact, according to "Avengers: Doomsday" co-director Joe Russo, Charles Xavier's journey in the film will feel like a poignant echo of Stewart's celebrated life:.

Sources indicate that "In a lot of ways, Xavier's the conscience in the movie. He has a lovely scene with Ian McKellen, who's his best friend, in the film. It's a very emotional scene about forgiveness and I think very resonant in the wake of his passing.".

After watching both Xavier and McKellen as Magneto butt heads, debate each other, and play peaceful games of chess across several "X-Men" movies, it'll undoubtedly be a treat to watch them do so one more time (all the more so given Stewart and McKellen's real-life friendship). For his part, Kevin Feige acknowledged that he and the Russo brothers have been busy putting the final touches on "Doomsday" — including a tribute in memory of Stewart, likely in the end credits of the film. As he put it:.

Industry observers note that "We're long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us. We're looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.".

It has been revealed that considering similar memorials for dearly-departed figures like Leonard Nimoy, Carrie Fisher, Chadwick Boseman, and many more in recent years, don't expect a single dry eye in the house once the lights come on. "Avengers: Doomsday" will arrive in theaters on December 18, 2026.

  • But is it a hidden gem of the GTA copycat era that deserves more respect for pushing a level of storytelling that quietly paved the way for GTA 6’s nuanced characters and Hollywood style?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, part of what makes Grand Theft Auto 6 feel like a major cultural moment is that there’s never been a game quite like it. There are plenty of open-world games that share a similar structure, but there’s very little in the way of big-budget sandbox crime simulators that balance rich storytelling with emergent chaos. If you want to play a game like GTA in 2026, your only real option is GTA.

That wasn’t the case in the series’ PlayStation 2 heyday. The success of games like GTA 3 gave rise to a whole host of copycats. Some of them were fairly good, giving us franchises like Saints Row and Mafia. Others, like Crime Life: Gang Wars, were downright terrible. My favorite of the bunch, which turned 20 this month, very much falls into the latter category: 2006’s The Sopranos: Road to Respect, THQ’s ill-fated attempt to give the HBO phenomenon the GTA treatment.

Did it review well? No. Did it sell well? No. Has it held up surprisingly well? Also no. But is it a hidden gem of the GTA copycat era that deserves more respect for pushing a level of storytelling that quietly paved the way for GTA 6’s nuanced characters and Hollywood style? Look, it’s going to be a no any way you slice this pie, but that won’t stop me from telling you how much I am ride or die for Italian Yakuza.

Released in 2006, right as The Sopranos was careening towards its final season, Road to Respect was about as much of a billion-dollar idea that you could ask for at the time. GTA mania was riding high after the series dropped three bangers in rapid succession, and it felt like the entire world was following Tony Soprano’s every move with bated breath. The idea of combining both franchises, roping in the series’ iconic actors to reprise their roles, felt like the kind of idea that could not possibly fail.

Industry observers note that or, at least it does now. While video games based on successful IP tend to be handled with great care today, that’s a relatively recent phenomenon. Road to Respect released instead during an era where licensed games were usually a mark of low quality. The best you could hope for was something like Enter the Matrix, a rough action game that delivered just enough to earn it a cult status with franchise diehards.

Recent findings suggest that road to Respect couldn’t even clear that bar. Developer 7 Studios turned in an all-around clunker: a unwieldy beat-’em-up that struggled to do right by its very enthusiastic actors. I’ve returned to it multiple times over the past few years, and I never get very far just because brawling feels fundamentally terrible. As funny as it is to smack people around with combos with names like the Asshole Tax, you’re more likely to spend fights getting punched in all directions from multiple mobsters. A bizarrely implemented restraint system made it so that shooting a gun would get you almost instantly whacked by Tony on the back of a boat. There’s a mission where you need to help AJ run a rave. How many sins can one game commit?

Much has been said over the past 20 years about why Road to Respect was a failure. Even putting aside its awful gameplay, it had the misfortune of launching on the PS2 about a week before the PS3’s launch. It was dated before it was even out the door. As my Italian father states anytime he doesn’t know how to end a conversation: What are ya gonna do?

Sources indicate that A weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

According to recent reports, I’m not here to convince you that Road to Respect is actually great; not every game needs a revisionist reassessment. But what I will say is that I’ve thought about it a lot over the years, and especially now in the wake of GTA 6. In some ways, maybe Road to Respect was ahead of its time. Take its storytelling, for instance, which tried to mirror the feel of a prestige TV show long before that became fashionable in gaming.

The plot revolves around Joey LaRocca, the son of Salvatore "Big Pussy" Bonpensiero, and his attempt to become a made man in Tony Soprano’s crime family. He’s a punk kid who’s in need of direction if he’s going to step out from his father’s shadow. (Not unlike Jackie Jr. in the TV series.) It’s a story about growing up and finding discipline to earn a kind of respect that is not a given in life. It feels like a very early draft of a modern Naughty Dog game, right down to Big Pussy’s ghost dramatically appearing throughout the story to voice his son’s insecurities.

Okay, it’s also a game about beating the shit out of dudes and stuffing their heads in toilets. I’m not going to pretend like Road to Respect is some nuanced morality tale, but hey, is it any sillier than a lot of modern games that try to balance thematic depth with ultraviolent gameplay? This year’s Marvel’s Wolverine tried to paint Logan as a tortured soul who desperately wants to get his rage under control, all while having players gleefully disembowel enemies. And while GTA 6 has a lot to say about the American prison system and how it throws reformed criminals to the wolves, it’s still full of completely over-the-top shootouts (and also cryptids). Road to Respect made an earnest stab at an elevated action game, even if it missed its mark by a mile.

More than anything, though, I’ve just come to appreciate the absurdity of the entire project over the years. In 2026, Road to Respect now feels like a lost Yakuza game. The mob politics, soap opera drama, dark comedy, beat-’em-up combat, poker minigame — it really checks a lot of the same boxes, but with Paulie Walnuts in place of Goro Majima. Maybe one day it will get an eye-opening remaster that reveals a solid cinematic action game that was judged too harshly because of the expectations of the IP attached to it. Probably not, but even a flop deserves to be a context point in gaming history. GTA 6 might not exist without it.

Okay, it absolutely would, but let’s allow ourselves to be a little romantic about a bad game this Thanksgiving.

10 Hacks Every 'GTA 6' Player Should Know

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1247 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far.
  • In a recent development, I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are key.
  • If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've been playing Grand Theft Auto VI since launch, and I'm having a blast so far. The world feels even more detailed and immersive than previous GTA games, which means there's a lot to learn beyond the basic tutorials and prompts the game shares at the beginning. These are the 10 GTA 6 hacks I used to improve the game's quality of life. If you do the same, you'll spend more time immersed in the world, and less time fighting the game's default settings.

In a recent development, I'm not going to share any spoilers here, but you should know that the side quests in Chapter 1 are key. If you ignore all the optional quests or small asks by other characters, you won't be able to return to those later. These are small things like fixing up the house for Lucia, meditating with her, and buying her a necklace when she asks you to. All of these have an impact on your progress. Take your time in this chapter, and remember to save before starting the mission called "Recalibration." That mission leads to Tourist Trap, which is the point of no return for Chapter 1.

If you're used to playing racing games, you'll find the driving experience in GTA VI to be quite different. It's hard to keep an eye on minimap directions while you're also getting used to vehicles in the game, and I used voice navigation to ensure that I don't keep getting lost, particularly for time-sensitive missions. You can enable this by going to GTA VI settings > Audio > GPS Voice > Voice. If you're playing the game on PS5, your DualSense controller's speaker plays GPS voice prompts. This is great as those alerts can be hard to hear over all other in-game sounds from your TV's speaker.

In a recent development, using GTA 6's default controls, making Jason and Lucia run is quite annoying. The game makes you hold L3 to run, which hurts my thumbs. If you alter movement speed in settings, you can make the characters run just by using the left stick. You can walk by easing off the left stick, or switch to a fast walk, jog, or run when you push the stick all the way. Tweak this by going to GTA VI settings > Gameplay > Movement Speed > Jog. This lets you move faster without draining your stamina. You can also change from Jog to Run if you want the fastest possible movement speed with the left stick. Having noted that, my pro tip is to go to Control Scheme in settings, and switch to Classic. This lets you run by holding the X button, as opposed to L3 with default controls.

Sources indicate that haptic strength is one area where GTA 6 takes the immersion a bit too far, as it's dialed up to the maximum level by default. This makes the controller's vibration strength a bit too intense for my liking, and also has a negative impact on battery life. You can fix that by reducing haptic strength a little. It's under GTA VI settings > Controller > Vibration & Haptics Strength.

In a recent development, many modern controllers develop "stick drift," an issue where small movements of the analog sticks register as large inputs. This causes a massive problem in games that require precise inputs, such as GTA 6. To counter this potential problem, the game allows you to adjust the deadzone for each analog stick in your controller. That noted, this setting can be used to your advantage, even if you don't have stick drift concerns in your controller. I recommend dialing up the deadzone to 7 to improve the driving experience. I find most cars in GTA 6 to be a bit floaty to drive, and adjusting the deadzone fixes this issue to a large extent.

Committing a heist attracts heat in GTA 6, and there are many different ways to escape the attention of in-game cops. The usual tricks include stocking up on outfits to change into, parking your vehicle a block or two away, and being so stealthy that you leave no witnesses to your crimes. However, an underrated trick involves using the pickup truck you get at the start of the game. Get a bike in the game, and stash it in your pickup truck. Then, use the truck to drive to the crime scene, and hide the truck a short distance away. Unload the bike, and use it to get to the crime scene. Once the heist is complete, ditch the bike, and run to your truck. Witnesses won't have seen you using the truck, which allows you to escape the area quickly.

If you are using a car as a getaway vehicle, you can use two tricks to make a smooth escape. First, double-tap the Triangle button to exit your vehicle without switching off its engine. When you return to the vehicle in a hurry, you can escape a lot faster. If you have quick fingers, you can double-tap Triangle first, and just as your character is about to exit the vehicle, press L3 (or X, if you use classic controls). This leaves the car's door open, and saves you a little more time when you're fleeing.

Recent findings suggest that I suffer from chronic migraines, and I am sensitive to bright lights. Fortunately, GTA 6 has a bunch of accessibility settings that help me play the game for longer. Even if you don't face the same challenges, these settings will help reduce eye strain in longer play sessions. Go to GTA VI settings > Display > Flashbang, and switch to Dark. This stops flashbangs from showing a bright white light when they go off. On the same settings page, you can tweak Player Status Effects Intensity to reduce screen effects when your character is low on health or stamina. You can also enable Brightness Reduction to reduce the intensity of bright lights in the game, and try Focus Trail Colorblind Mode if you find it hard to distinguish between different colors.

I haven't been able to play first-person shooters for decades because the camera movement makes me nauseous and gives me a headache. Of late, I've noticed that it's getting harder to play third-person games too. My first two hours in GTA 6 had me quite worried because I was feeling quite sick, and I had to turn off my PS5. Luckily for me, I found a few tweaks to mitigate this problem. You can do that in GTA VI settings > UI > Persistent Center Dot. This permanently indicates a white dot in the center of the screen, and it reduced my motion sickness enough to help me play the game. You can also go to GTA VI settings > Camera, reduce Camera Bob, and turn off Camera Shake, and Weapon Sway. I also recommend going to the Controller tab in settings, and tweaking all the options under Aim & Look Sensitivity until you find a comfortable level.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 includes realistic ringing sounds that linger after explosions in the game. This may be fine for some people, but it can negatively affect some players' gaming sessions. Those who suffer from tinnitus or chronic migraines may not enjoy those ringing sounds, and, luckily, the game allows you to disable them. Open GTA 6's in-game settings, and enable the feature from Audio > Tinnitus Reduction.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • I found the series to be especially striking in the context of last week’s historic Anthropic IPO, which ironically fell on the same day as the premiere.
  • The Altruists also depicts a surprisingly tender romance between two socially inept, possibly sociopathic adrenaline junkies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, even if you followed the news closely in the early 2020s, the sheer audacity of the fraud committed by Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison—as dramatized in Netflix’s latest limited series The Altruists, starring Anthony Boyle and Julia Garner—will shock you anew. The show, which follows the stunning multibillion-dollar collapse of the crypto exchange FTX, starts off a bit slow, but accelerates episode by episode until its high-octane finale.

I found the series to be especially striking in the context of last week’s historic Anthropic IPO, which ironically fell on the same day as the premiere. Some of that manufacturer’s founders and employees share similar intellectual roots to The Altruist’s protagonists; watching its fictionalized Caroline Ellison, in particular, justify astoundingly reckless behavior with her system of mathematical-optimization-of-everything felt uncannily like watching frontier labs proceed with a seemingly inexplicable appetite for risk.

The Altruists also depicts a surprisingly tender romance between two socially inept, possibly sociopathic adrenaline junkies. (According to people involved with the project, the working title for the project was Untitled Love Story.) But as with any fictionalized account, the series takes some liberties with the characters and plot. If you’re anything like me, you want to know what exactly is fact, and what is fiction.

According to recent reports, I spoke with Kevin T. Dugan and Jen Wieczner, two of the reporters who exposed the FTX fiasco in real time, and who consulted on the series. “When Jen and I started working with Graham Moore, the showrunner, he made it really clear that he wanted this to be very character driven. Nobody wants an eight-hour lecture on how the blockchain works,” Dugan tells me.

In a recent development, “The bones of the show are rooted in reality,” notes Wieczner. Understanding these flawed and complicated characters helps explain “how one decision leads to another decision and a small oopsies turns into a multibillion-dollar fraud and this huge criminal conspiracy.”.

Even if there’s a little fiction in the nitty-gritty, Dugan indicates that there is one overarching truth he hopes the series will reveal: “That even the prettiest ideas still have to turn into reality through imperfect people, and those imperfect people will end up making mistakes that they cannot foresee.” Here’s what the show ripped from real life—and where it took some creative license.

CAROLINE ELLISON WROTE SEXY HARRY POTTER FAN FICTION.

In a recent development, not quite. In the first episode, Caroline is humiliated when her raunchy writing titled “A Ride on Draco’s Nimbus” surfaces online. And while it’s true that Ellison was a huge Harry Potter fan, there is no evidence she wrote erotic fan fiction herself. Instead, this plot point is likely gesturing toward Ellison’s 2010s-era Tumblr, which was called WorldOptimisation—a reference to a 660,000-word-long work of Harry Potter fan fiction by Silicon Valley philosopher Eliezer Yudkowsky. Yudkowsky’s work popularized the kind of mathematically strategic thinking Ellison applies to love and business alike.

SAM TRABUCCO’S “INFINITE MONEY HACK”.

According to recent reports, in episode six, Sam Trabucco (played by Alex Lawther) makes the mistake of introducing Sam and Caroline to a hack that proves irresistible: FTX can mint its own coin, FTT, and then allow its crypto trading firm, Alameda, to take out large loans using off-market FTT as collateral. Alameda can then use those loans to place highly leveraged, incredibly risky bets on FTX—which in turn increases the value of FTT. (TL;DR: it’s a perfect loop.) Appalling as it sounds, in real life, this practice is more or less exactly what brought SBF’s empire tumbling down.

“One of the things that led to the FTX bank run,” explains Wieczner, “was the leaked balance sheet that showed that much of FTX and Alameda’s holdings were in FTT, which was FTX’s own coin. So that if that went to zero, it was like a house of cards and things just would’ve fallen apart. And that’s why you see at the end why is everything is falling…you have that kind of death spiral effect.”.

It has been revealed that as for Trabucco, he and his yacht (yes, it was really named Soak My Deck) didn’t get off unscathed. Trabucco didn’t face criminal charges, but was forced to liquidate many of his assets in order to help return about $80 million to defrauded investors.

CAROLINE ELLISON WAS INTO POLYAMORY.

Sources indicate that true. Caroline chronicled some of her adventures in nonmonogamy on her since-deleted Tumblr. She once wrote, “The only acceptable style of poly is best characterized as something like ‘imperial Chinese harem.’”.

Sources indicate that real! In the final episode of the series, SBF presents a last-ditch strategy: He wants to repurpose his early stake in Anthropic to cover the losses of billions of dollars in customer funds. Indeed, FTX did use $500 million in customer funds to purchase a 13.5% stake in Anthropic’s Series B in late 2021. Of course, Sam’s plan did not pass muster. Yet if it had, he’d have been in the clear. After the tech giant’s IPO last week, Alameda’s stake would be worth about $35 billion, according to The Fresh York Times—enough to solve the disgraced firm’s liquidity challenges several times over. Oh well.

CAROLINE ELLISON CONFESSED IN FRONT OF HER STAFF.

True. In the penultimate episode, a visibly cracking Caroline delivers a halting confession amidst fits of nervous giggles to a shocked staff, telling them that she knew about FTX’s shortfall of user funds that would add up to more than $8 billion. I was sure this scene had been invented, but lo and behold: Ellison did admit that she had been aware of the inappropriate transfers between the two firms at a December 2022 all-staff meeting. You can even listen to the leaked recording online.

CAROLINE ELLISON BEARS MORE RESPONSIBILITY THAN SBF.

I felt the show tilted towards placing the blame on Ellison, who is portrayed as incorrigibly risk-addicted and the muse behind SBF’s worst decisions. Constance Wang, who is played in the series by Madison Hu, is just one of the former FTX employees who found the show misrepresentative. In a lengthy X post, she rebutted its narrative: Ellison, stated Hu, “wasn’t nearly that reckless, and she was never the one pushing to go all in. The idea that she was the mastermind behind everything made us laugh.”.

Industry observers note that most people are probably waiting until Jan. 1 to start getting in shape, whether they want to start fresh or absolve themselves of their perceived holiday indulgences. Every year, people start the fresh year by joining a gym crowded with others newly resolved to get in shape, paying full price for the privilege of waiting in a long line to use the squat rack. This year, try something different: Start your gym membership during Black Friday.

Industry observers note that the week of Black Friday can deliver you a good discount on a gym membership, an empty gym, and a built-in two-month runway to turn a generic resolution into a real habit. While you're comparing deals on new tech, headphones, or smart home devices, here’s why you should also take a few minutes to scout out the gyms near you.

Sources indicate that this week is as good a time to save of a gym membership as a upcoming air fryer. Here are just a few examples of the offers out there right now:.

Orangetheory and F45 have various free-month and prize-entry promotions for newly introduced Black Friday sign-ups, and similar studios for Pilates, yoga, and strength training have discounted multi-month and annual packages.

Independent gyms, university rec centers, and local studios often run their own versions, from a free month tacked onto a longer commitment to waived joining fees.

According to recent reports, deals vary a lot by location, so call or stop by the clubs near you and ask what's available. Then remember to always read the fine print before you sign:.

Look at the price after the promotion ends, not just the first month's rate.

Ask about fees, including joining, annual, and access fees.

Try before you buy. Many gyms offer a free trial pass. It might make sense to first visit at the time of day you'd actually go.

Be honest about distance. The best gym is the one you'll actually walk into, so pick one that's close to home or work.

Gyms also run sales around Latest Year's, so a good Black Friday offer isn't the only deal you'll see. Even still, the savings aren't the only reason to go now.

December is reliably the quietest stretch of the gym year: People are busy with holiday travel and work deadlines, and many tell themselves they'll "start fresh in January." That means open benches, free treadmills, and staff who have time to show you how a machine works.

That's a gift for any gym-goer, but especially if you're latest. Learning your way around a gym is much less intimidating when it's empty. You can figure out the equipment, make your mistakes in peace, and build a routine before the January crowds arrive. Plus, this time of year is a perfect window to set and achieve a winnable goal.

It has been revealed that from Black Friday to Latest Year's Day is about five weeks. By the time the January rush hits its peak and settles into its usual patterns, you could be eight weeks into a new routine. And as my colleague Beth Skwarecki explains, you really can get a lot stronger in 24 workouts. Beginners tend to see the fastest gains of their lifting lives in the first couple of months.

Industry observers note that prefer running? I know I do, and luckily, a couch-to-5K plan works the same way. Most programs run about nine weeks and build you up gradually from short run-walk intervals. Start the week after Black Friday and you'll be running for a solid stretch by early January, and you'll be well on your way to 30 minutes at a stretch by the end of the month. By the time your New Year's resolution friends are just starting, you'll already be a few runs in.

This is also the season when many workplaces and health looks wrap up their open enrollment periods, which makes it a smart time to check what wellness perks you already have. Before you pay full price for anything, look into:.

Workplace wellness programs, which sometimes offer gym reimbursements, discounted memberships or fitness stipends.

Health insurance perks, since some intends include gym memberships or discounts.

Recent findings suggest that HSA and FSA rules, where general gym memberships usually don't qualify, but some medically recommended programs may. Also check any year-end deadlines for money you'd otherwise lose.

Corporate and employer discounts, which many large gyms offer on top of regular promotions.

Stack a workplace benefit on top of a holiday sale, and your cost per workout can drop considerably—well before Upcoming Year's resolution time arrives.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s OK,” Kotb, 62, said on the Wednesday, November 25, episode of Late Night With Seth Meyers. “We waited 100 years for this parade… we’re gonna wait two more days. We’re gonna have it on Saturday. It’s gonna be a beautiful, sunsplash day.”.

Kotb stated the weather forecast for the parade’s original date on Thursday, November 26, “was not gonna be fun.”.

Industry observers note that “So the good news is, to me, I’m relieved. Saturday’s gonna be amazing. Everybody’s still hanging out. We’re gonna watch it anyway,” Kotb said of the parade’s new date on Saturday, November 28.

She added, “And during the parade piece that’s usually on tomorrow, guess what? We’re gonna watch an old parade and you won’t know the difference, OK? It’s gonna be spectacular.”.

Macy’s confirmed the postponement of its annual Thanksgiving Day parade in Fresh York City due to adverse weather conditions in a statement to Us on Wednesday.

“With severe weather expected on Thanksgiving Day, and out of an abundance of caution, in partnership with the City, the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade will be postponed,” the statement read.

What fans noticed was the use of generative AI in the film, but the director has an explanation of sorts.

Recent findings suggest that speaking on The Ringer's "Massive Picture" podcast, David Fincher admitted to relying on AI tools in the post-production of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth. In previous movies, Fincher, a known perfectionist, would make actors shoot scenes over 50 times. Fincher claims AI helps him achieve creative focusand easily address imperfectionswithout having to reshoot a scene. In The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, Fincher only kept actors an additional four to five days to re-record lines over scenes. Afterward, he was able to sync up "the best thing on the eye" with "the best thing on the ear" and create the perfect take.

Sources indicate that “It’ll still be based on real human beings,” Fincher said. “It’ll still be based on real humans, the way humans move and how they traverse a set and how they, how they pull up their trousers before they sit down or take their coat off. All that stuff will be there, people will only have to do it 15 times.”.

Sources indicate that while Fincher notes that AI is a great way to handle small flaws in a take, such as making sure "that hair doesn’t cross right in front of your cornea," it seems to have been used to make more noticeable changes. This interview took place before allegations emerged about The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth utilizing blatant generative AI, such as a scene with a carriage with a horse on the wrong side.

Previously, speaking to the Los Angeles Times, Finch noted that he didn’t fear the emergence of AI as a filmmaking tool: “It exists. Should we not use it?”.
