📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is going to look a bit different.
  • The result is an epic 10-minute medley, introduced by Julianne Hough, who will star in Damn Yankees on Broadway this spring, featuring nine beloved Broadway shows: The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Disney’s Aladdin, Hamilton, The Lost Boys, Rent, Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show, Schmigadoon!, and—what else?—Wicked.
  • The mastermind behind the mega-medley is none other than Tom Kitt, the Tony-, Emmy-, Grammy-, and Pulitzer Prize–winning composer behind Next to Normal, If/Then, and Almost Famous.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is going to look a bit different. First, the threat of severe weather has prompted Macy’s to reschedule the event until Saturday, beginning at 8:30 a.m. ET. But even before the forecast turned, there was a big change: While in the past, viewers would enjoy five or so of the best performances from the current Broadway season, this year, there’s only one big Broadway number. But don’t fret, theater folk. For the milestone occasion of the parade’s 100th anniversary, the powers that be at NBC and Macy’s have put a new spin on their tried-and-true formula, gathering the Broadway community for one supersized performance, featuring more demonstrates and performers than ever before.

The result is an epic 10-minute medley, introduced by Julianne Hough, who will star in Damn Yankees on Broadway this spring, featuring nine beloved Broadway shows: The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Disney’s Aladdin, Hamilton, The Lost Boys, Rent, Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show, Schmigadoon!, and—what else?—Wicked.

The mastermind behind the mega-medley is none other than Tom Kitt, the Tony-, Emmy-, Grammy-, and Pulitzer Prize–winning composer behind Next to Normal, If/Then, and Almost Famous. Kitt is no stranger to writing a massive production number, having cowritten the Tony Awards opening number “Bigger!,” performed by host Neil Patrick Harris with lyrics by Lin-Manuel Miranda in 2013, among other ambitious musical endeavors. Despite his previous experience, a 10-minute, nine-show medley presented a unique set of challenges the composer had yet to tackle.

A total of 133 people are performing in the medley—114 Broadway cast members, 17 dancers, a child actor, and Hough. On top of that, more than 125 other Broadway professionals—including stage managers, wardrobe supervisors, and hair and makeup teams—are on site to facilitate the production, bringing the total number of people involved to well over 250.

Sources indicate that “Most key to me in doing something like this—to celebrate this community, this beautiful community that I’m so lucky to be a part of,” Kitt tells me. “Everyone who’s participating, you want them to feel happy and excited about what they’re doing.”.

According to recent reports, A little over a month ago, Kitt and creative producer Sarah O’Gleby got to work figuring out how to make a cohesive musical number out of nine very different shows. He wrote the first draft of the arrangement over the course of a few days. “It was way too long,” he claims. That might be because Kitt had to figure out how to connect these disparate shows musically while also finding room for Easter eggs for theater fans: musical nods to shows that might not otherwise be featured in the medley, including Anything Goes, The Music Man, A Chorus Line, and Kitt’s personal favorite, Into the Woods, whose music kicks things off.

Industry observers note that “Into the Woods was one of those shows that made me want to write for the theater,” he tells me. “The downbeat of the prologue is one of the most beautiful musical gestures; every time I hear it, I get goosebumps. So that was really special and notable for me to get to plug into, and there are so many others.”.

Surprisingly, it will be Kitt’s first time attending the parade in person. “The parade has meant so much to me,” he says. “I’ve watched it for years. I’ve taped it. I’m lucky enough to have reveals that have been a part of it. I think that celebrating that relationship and celebrating the history of Broadway and being able to spotlight so many notable shows and artists just feels very exciting and gratifying.”.

Industry observers note that “I’m a tiny little person, but I love to do really significant things,” says O’Gleby. A former performer on the West End, O’Gleby moved to the States almost two decades ago to pursue a career as a Broadway performer, dancing in revivals of Brigadoon and How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying. Now she choreographs Broadway productions like Shucked and, most recently, Pink’s widely celebrated Tony Awards opening number. Given her Broadway bona fides, she’s also intimately familiar with the magic of the parade. “I was lucky to perform on the parade as a Broadway girl and the associate choreographer and dance captain on shows that I was in,” she says. “It was so wonderfully American.”.

The first of two rehearsals took place Friday afternoon at Pier59 Studios at Chelsea Piers. Around 4 p.m., as the sun began to set over the Hudson River, Broadway performers from different shows practiced the medley. O’Gleby, wearing silver leather pants and clutching a God mic, was charged with organizing the chaos and managing the more than 100 Broadway performers in the room. Standing offstage between a broomstick and a red Les Mis flag, I could still see traces of green makeup on the face of Wicked’s current Elphaba, Keri René Fuller. Most of the performers gathered had a show of their own to perform in just a few hours, but that didn’t stop them from giving it their all in rehearsal, onstage and off, cheering the other productions along as each got its moment in the spotlight.

Recent findings suggest that case in point: At the end of the rehearsal, the whole room erupted into cheers for the original cast members from Rent—including original Angel, Tony winner Wilson Jermaine Heredia, and original Joanne, Fredi Walker—who are gathering to perform “Seasons of Love” in the parade. (During the rehearsal, Aladdin’s current Genie, Sherri Shepherd, couldn’t help but mouth along to the words of the seminal song.) “It was that moment of why we’re a part of this community,” O’Gleby states, nearly choking up. “Everyone in the room—stage managers, costume, I mean everybody in the room—the way they were applauding these original cast members and what they gave to all of us as a community, really all over the world, it was incredible.”.

According to recent reports, at the second rehearsal, on Monday night outside on 34th Street beneath Macy’s giant turkey, the mood remained high even as the temperatures dropped. By 11 p.m., performers were bundled in winter jackets, sweatshirts, and leg warmers, with their character shoes still on. They hugged one another for warmth and jumped up and down, kicking their feet to stay loose between setups. Margaret Cho, who stars as the Narrator in The Rocky Horror Show, danced “The Time Warp” with her Chihuahua, Lucia, tucked into a pouch in her jacket, the dog’s head peeking out.

According to recent reports, for O’Gleby, a smooth Monday-night rehearsal means setting each show up for success come Saturday morning and making sure all nine demonstrates are “represented in the most powerful and clear storytelling way that we can,” she says. “This is a huge moment for these shows to sell lots of tickets so everyone gets to keep making their magic every night. And so it’s notable to me that each team gets to communicate what they need and what they think would really make their show shine.”.

On Wednesday afternoon, Macy's declared that “after close consultation with our City and agency partners, we have made the decision to move this year’s celebration,” a disappointing piece of news for those who build their holiday around the annual event.

This is only the fourth time in history that the parade hasn't been held on Thanksgiving: In 1942, 1943, and 1944 it was canceled completely as its trademark giant balloons were repurposed as part of the World War II effort. Compared to those years, a move to Saturday seems manageable, O’Gleby says. “The weather will be what it will be, but we will delight in that and deliver the best.".

Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1466 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you or someone on your shopping list wants a newly introduced smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from.
  • There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark.
  • Industry observers note that contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you or someone on your shopping list wants a newly introduced smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from. The problem is, a lot of them can be quite pricey. Apple's cheapest smartwatch, the SE 3, starts at $249, and its other selections only skyrocket from there. On the flip side, the risk in picking a smartwatch that's too inexpensive is that the manufacturer likely made a series of sacrifices to get the price that low. At a certain point, the tradeoff just isn't worth it.

Luckily, you do have options. There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark. And while you shouldn't expect the same capabilities as you would on flagship wearables, these devices are perfectly usable, both as fitness trackers and smartwatches—all while spending well below $100 a pop. CNET put both smartwatches through their paces to make these determinations, so you know whichever model you get, you won't be picking up a wearable paperweight.

Industry observers note that contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter. Amazfit is its own organization, and produces a wide selection of smartwatch options. The Bip 6 happens to be the company's latest budget smartwatch, with an MSRP of just $79.99. In most cases, a price that low would be a red flag for a smartwatch, but not in the Bip 6's case.

The Amazfit Bip 6 holds its own against other flagship smartwatches. That's true on a surface level: This watch looks your average smartwatch, rather than a cheap imitation. In fact, at first glance, I'd bet most people would assume the Bip 6 is actually an Apple Watch. It has a rounded square design with a large 1.97-inch display with a resolution of 390 by 450 pixels (though there's no Always-On display). This isn't a cheap display, either: Amazfit put an AMOLED screen on the watch, which looks great indoors—though CNET Labs struggled to see the screen in direct sunlight.

In a recent development, where the Bip 6 really shines, however, is with fitness tracking. This watch supports GPS, which makes tracking outdoor runs possible without a smartphone. CNET Labs found that it takes about 10 seconds to find a GPS signal, but once it connects, you're set. While running, the Bip 6 reliably tracks your heart rate. CNET Labs compared its sensor to the Polar chest strap HR monitor and found it on par, though, like other smartwatches, the Bip 6 is slower at detecting heart rate spikes. You'll get data like cadence and stride while tracking runs, and strength training and muscle groups while working out indoors. For example, CNET Labs found that it correctly identified arm muscle exercises while testing the watch during a pilates session.

In a recent development, you also get some health and wellness features, too. The Bip 6 can measure heart rate variations, body temperature changes, sleep stages, and even your breathing quality. Its One Tap Measuring mode supports a single reading for heart rate, SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation), stress, and breathing rate, and it supports cycle tracking—though CNET specifies it can't track skin temperature like other smartwatches and health trackers. There's an optional subscription that provides AI coaching tools and looks out for health conditions like sleep apnea and insomnia. While health and wellness tracking is solid, note that CNET Labs found Amazfit's app, Zepp, to be confusing, since it simply displays your data without much context or explanation.

For an $80 smartwatch, the Bip 6 has an excellent battery life. CNET Labs found that the watch could be pushed to its limits—multiple workouts using GPS, heart rate tracking, keeping the display on during workouts—and still run for eight days before needing a charge. In fact, reviewer Vanessa Hand Orellana speculates you could push the Bip 6 to Amazfit's two-week battery life claim by limiting some of the most intensive settings and features. The only downside here is that there is no fast charging, so it will take about two hours to get back to 100%. But if you're only charging the watch once every week or two, that isn't much of a burden. There's also no charger in the box, so you'll need to use a separate USB-C cable.

As a smartwatch, the Bip 6 can be a mixed bag. CNET found that the UI was clunky and sluggish, and the OS requires some user intervention before it's as usable as a standard Apple Watch or Galaxy Watch. While the watch has a voice assistant, Flow, CNET found it to be borderline unusable. However, CNET says Android owners can reply to texts with a keyboard or dictation without needing the assistant. iPhone users can't do the same by default, but by downloading a third-party app, they can jerry-rig the watch to send and receive texts.

In a recent development, based on CNET Labs' testing, the Amazfit Bip 6 is one of the best budget smartwatches you can buy. For $80, you get a reliable workout tracker that looks like most standard watches on the market. And while you're making some sacrifices at this price point, they're largely worth it for $80.

Recent findings suggest that while the Amazfit is a good choice for both iPhone and Android consumers, the Galaxy Fit 3 might be the best choice for Samsung users. This isn't an option for iPhone users, and while it works with all Android devices, you get some Samsung-specific perks if you have a Galaxy phone.

Sources indicate that the Galaxy Fit 3 is even cheaper than the Amazfit Bip 6: This watch is only $60, which makes it among the cheapest smartwatches you can buy. Now, this doesn't look like your average smartwatch. Samsung opted for a fitness tracker-like design, with a long 1.6-inch (40mm) AMOLED display. But for a fitness tracker/smartwatch hybrid, it's a solid look.

In CNET's testing, one of the Galaxy Fit 3's biggest strengths is its battery life—though it pales in comparison to the Bip 6. When pushed to its limits, the Fit 3 can run three days in between charges, though Samsung claims you can get it up to 13 days with the right settings. While the Amazfit has it beat, the Fit 3 might sound like a dream compared to other smartwatches, even from Samsung. Unlike the Bip 6, the Fit 3 supports fast charging. You can fill the watch up completely in just over an hour.

Sources indicate that CNET did find that the "smart" elements of this wearable were a bit lacking, however. The Fit 3 doesn't support voice dictation or mobile payments like other watches do, and unless you have a Galaxy phone, you won't be able to access the camera remote or sync your alarms. And while the Amazfit Bip 6's "Flow" is hardly reliable, the Fit 3 doesn't have an assistant at all. You can see incoming calls and decline (but not answer) them, and you can send prewritten responses to text messages, but not initiate them. Still, CNET found that Samsung added the essentials: You have an alarm, calculator, weather app, camera remote, and, of course, the Samsung Health app. (What kind of health tracker would this be without it?).

It has been revealed that CNET found that the Fit 3 is a reliable fitness tracker, particularly for $60. You can track over 100 different workouts, and the watch automatically logs exercises like runs, walks, rowing, and elliptical sessions—if you enable auto-tracking, that is. It also supports swimming with its IP68 water resistance rating. CNET Labs found that the heart rate tracking was "generally accurate" when compared to the Polar chest strap, though its slower with registering heart rate spikes. Interestingly, the heart rate tracker was a bit delayed in testing, but once CNET reviewed the data in the health app, the data had corrected to be largely accurate. You also get high and low heart rate alerts, though no ECG app. (The $249 Apple Watch SE 3 also omits this feature.).

In CNET's testing, the sleep tracker on the Fit 3 was useful, if not entirely accurate. The watch can detect your sleep stages and look out for snoring using your Galaxy phone's mic. Like other health trackers, you get a sleep score, but CNET found it a bit inaccurate, since it rated a six and a half hour sleep session "Excellent" (91/100).

According to recent reports, still, the Fit 3 is really the only other smartwatch option at this price point that people should seriously consider. Until another company drops a product around this MSRP, you have two solid choices in the Amazfit Bip 6 and Galaxy Fit 3.

Industry News: Avengers: Secret Wars Setting Confirmed By Marvel, Spoiling Doomsday

💡 Key Takeaways

The final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer promises a major showdown between Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom and a conglomerate of heroes from various timelines.
  • We've known for some time that one of Marvel Comics' greatest modern writers, Jonathan Hickman, is a secret MCU consultant, and that "Avengers: Doomsday" is loosely adapting his "Avengers: Time Runs Out" storyline from 2014.
  • Industry observers note that the Marvel Studios president told the outlet, "'Secret Wars' is different than any other movie we've ever made.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it looks like we're heading to the Marvel Cinematic Universe's version of Battleworld in "Avengers: Secret Wars." The final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer promises a major showdown between Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor von Doom and a conglomerate of heroes from various timelines. As it stands, "Doomsday" has a real shot at the biggest box office opening weekend ever, which would bode very well for the second part of Joe and Anthony Russo's upcoming duology, "Avengers: Secret Wars." That sequel is due out on December 17, 2027, and if "Doomsday" does what "Infinity War" did back in 2018, it should have a grand old time at the box office. That is, if Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige doesn't spoil things before then.

We've known for some time that one of Marvel Comics' greatest modern writers, Jonathan Hickman, is a secret MCU consultant, and that "Avengers: Doomsday" is loosely adapting his "Avengers: Time Runs Out" storyline from 2014. That arc serves as a prelude to Hickman's 2015 "Secret Wars" storyline, and together these two runs see the Marvel universe collapse due to "incursions," after which Victor von Doom uses fragments of the shattered multiverse to create a upcoming planet named Battleworld. In an interview with Entertainment Weekly, Feige basically confirmed that this is the setting for the MCU's version of "Secret Wars," basically spoiling "Doomsday" by strongly hinting how that film ends and where the next one begins.

Industry observers note that the Marvel Studios president told the outlet, "'Secret Wars' is different than any other movie we've ever made. Look at the comics. The characters and the settings and the worlds within this singular planet where our movie 'Secret Wars' takes place is the imagination gone wild, which is what's exciting about it." So there you have it. Most fans expected to see Battleworld in "Secret Wars," but now it's as close to official as you can get.

It has been revealed that the first "Secret Wars" comic book arc arrived in 1984, with writer Jim Shooter and artists Mike Zeck and Bob Layton delivering a story in which the cosmic entity known as The Beyonder forced various Marvel characters to fight to the death on the planet Battleworld. It seems Marvel Studios will draw from this original run for some aspects of "Avengers: Doomsday" and "Avengers: Secret Wars." But for the most part, Jonathan Hickman's 2015 run serves as the basis for the two movies.

Recent findings suggest that this second "Secret Wars" arc, illustrated by artist Esad Ribić with cover designs by Alex Ross, and the run that preceded it, "Time Runs Out," are the essential inspiration for "Doomsday" and its sequel. Feige told Entertainment Weekly that "Doomsday" is basically the MCU's version of "Time Runs Out," while the filmmakers described "Secret Wars" as "a little bit of both" that storyline and Hickman's "Secret Wars.".

Recent findings suggest that asked to comment further, Feige remarked, "If you wanted spoilers for 'The Odyssey,' you could go read the book. If you want spoilers for 'Doomsday' and 'Secret Wars,' you can go look at the comics," adding, "It is very much the same thing that we're doing." Clearly, then, Hickman's work is integral to the two upcoming MCU releases, with Feige going on to say that "Secret Wars" is "very much" the "culmination of an incursion, multiversal-collapse event." With that in mind, you can bet the "Doomsday" sequel will play out pretty much entirely on the MCU's version of Battleworld, with the surviving heroes from "Doomsday" taking the fight to its god emperor, Doom, in an attempt to overthrow his regime and restore the multiverse. Whether "Secret Wars" will include Marvel's infamous Spider-Man bathroom scene, however, remains unconfirmed.

None of Kevin Feige's latest revelations should come as a major shock to Marvel fans who've known Marvel Studios has been drawing from Jonathan Hickman's "Secret Wars" run. But this is the closest Feige has come to officially confirming Battleworld as the setting for "Avengers: Secret Wars." The Marvel Studios head didn't use the name "Battleworld," but his comments about a "singular planet" were in response to a question about it.

Otherwise, Feige characterized "Avengers: Doomsday" as "a culmination of what's come before," and "Secret Wars" as "a launching pad for [Marvel Studios'] films in 2028 — the 20th anniversary of the MCU." Clearly, then, whatever happens at the end of "Secret Wars" will set the stage for newly introduced characters, timelines, and storylines that will reshape the way the MCU looks going forward.

Sources indicate that we know that Marvel Studios is preparing its Jake Schrier-directed X-Men movie, which is set to debut in the wake of "Secret Wars." First, though, Marvel is reworking its cinematic universe with "Doomsday" and "Secret Wars." According to co-director Joe Russo, this simply had to be done with two movies due to it being "such a major storyline." He continued: "Doom as a character needs a lot of space, especially when Robert Downey is playing him. So the scale of the story, the emotional scale of the story is so large that it really needed to be a two-parter.".

Whether the second part of that two-parter will actually debut on December 17, 2027, however, remains unclear. Production on "Secret Wars" has been moved to 2027, suggesting a delay might be imminent. For now, we'll have to wait and see how things play out. But regardless of when the movie actually arrives, prepare yourselves for a substantial screen visit to Battleworld.

Three Reasons Not to Use ‘Buy Now, Pay Later’ During Black Friday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales.
  • While BNPL intends can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any massive discounts.
  • To be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the tech giant is not uniquely misleading on this front.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales. As you're adding item after item to your cart during the sale, you might be tempted by offers for an "affordable monthly payment system." Also known as "buy now, pay later" (BNPL), the pitch is a tempting one: Buy what you need now, and pay later, "on your own timeline." But as convenient as it sounds, you should think twice before using buy now, pay later options, whether during Black Friday, Cyber Monday, or at any other time.

While BNPL intends can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any massive discounts. Let's take a look at the hidden costs of BNPL, and why you're better off paying upfront for all your Black Friday purchases.

To be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the tech giant is not uniquely misleading on this front. The process is straightforward: you choose your items, select Affirm (a third-party lender) at checkout, complete a quick application, and receive an instant decision on your loan terms. Individual transactions initiated through Affirm are limited to $25,000, with a daily maximum of $100,000 across multiple purchases—but of course, your Black Friday splurge will be nowhere near that big, right? (Right?!).

Sources indicate that the main draw of these programs is the ability to "pay at your own pace." If you are required to pay a down payment, that is due at the time of the transaction. From there, your first monthly payment is usually due one month after your purchase is processed. Each following payment will be due one month later, on the same day of the month.

You can choose your own timeline, usually spanning 3, 6, 12, or 24 months, depending on the purchase amount and your creditworthiness. Unlike traditional credit cards, Affirm demonstrates you the exact payment amount and total cost upfront, and claims no hidden fees or compound interest.

You need a separate Affirm account in addition to your Amazon Prime membership. The application process requires basic information, including your name, mobile phone number, date of birth, and the last four digits of your Social Security number. Affirm performs a soft credit check initially, which doesn't impact your credit score, though they may conduct a hard inquiry for some loans.

BNPL plans are helpful if you really need to finance something big, but whenever possible, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses.

The ease of this sort of financing can make expensive purchases feel more affordable than they actually are. When you can buy a $1,000 tablet for "just $67 per month," it's easy to lose sight of the total cost, as well as your overall financial picture. In turn, this makes it all too easy to overspend on items you might not have purchased otherwise. You're better off taking a breath, stepping away from your shopping cart, and setting alerts to be notified when a product hits a price you can stomach, at a time you can afford it.

Recent findings suggest that despite what you may have heard in the past, BNPL providers may report to credit bureaus, meaning your BNPL purchases can in fact affect your credit score. For instance, all Affirm payments (including on-time, late, and missed payments) are now reported to the credit bureau Experian. So if you miss payments or default on the installment strategy, it will cause damage to your credit score—making it even harder to get approved for mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and other financing down the road.

Still, not all BNPL providers report to credit bureaus or use the same type of credit check, so it’s important to understand the specific terms and practices of any service you’re considering.

Sources indicate that when you use a credit card, you get valuable purchase protections like extended warranty coverage, price protection, and the ability to dispute fraudulent charges. BNPL intends generally don't come with these safeguards. This means you're on the hook if something goes wrong with your BNPL purchase and the retailer doesn't make things right. The smarter move is to only buy what you can afford during a sale, no matter how tempting those deals may seem.

Although installment plans are helpful if you really need to finance something major, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses. Better to wait for a good price for something you truly need and can afford to pay for right now.

If there's a big-ticket item on sale for Black Friday but it's still out of your budget, consider these two questions before you turn to BNPL through Affirm:.

Is this really an essential purchase? BNPL should really only be used on completely necessary purchases that you can’t afford right now, but can afford in six weeks. On that note...

Industry observers note that will I be able to pay this off within six weeks? When a bigger payment gets broken down into smaller installments, you might find yourself overspending in the long run, because it "feels" like you can afford it. Stay on top of how much you’re actually spending—especially if you're considering multiple BNPL purchases—and how it will impact your overall budget going forward.

For more information about deals and discounts, keep an eye on all of Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage.

According to recent reports, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Industry observers note that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

In a recent development, the best thing you can do is compare the prices with other retailers that have Black Friday sales. If that seems like too much work, you can just follow our Black Friday coverage (we're already doing all the searching and vetting for you). Some other tips are making sure you're not being sold an older or cheaper version and always reading reviews.

How Blade Runner 2099 Took Inspiration From Denis Villeneuve's Legacy Sequel [Exclusive]

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's impossible enough to have to live in the shadow of an unabashed classic of cinema, so just imagine dealing with two of them.
  • Sources indicate that for showrunner Silka Luisa, this could've required one of two different approaches: stay suffocatingly faithful to the look and feel and tone of the two films or purposefully set off in the opposite direction.
  • "I knew we were definitely going to have an opportunity to lay our own track, because — it's right in the title, the fact that you're so many years past 2049, it gives you enough space to really carve out your own identity.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's impossible enough to have to live in the shadow of an unabashed classic of cinema, so just imagine dealing with two of them. There aren't many who would have a bad word to say about Ridley Scott's original "Blade Runner (well, except for those unfortunate critics who dismissed it upon release), but Denis Villeneuve's highly-acclaimed sequel "Blade Runner 2049" ain't too shabby, either. Now, Prime Video's "Blade Runner 2099" series has the added responsibility of picking up the story where its beloved predecessors left off ... along with all the pressure that comes with that.

Sources indicate that for showrunner Silka Luisa, this could've required one of two different approaches: stay suffocatingly faithful to the look and feel and tone of the two films or purposefully set off in the opposite direction. Well, in this case, how about a secret third option instead? During a recent press junket for "Blade Runner 2099," I spoke with Luisa over Zoom about where this show fits in next to its movie kin and how it finds its own niche amid a much wider world:.

"I knew we were definitely going to have an opportunity to lay our own track, because — it's right in the title, the fact that you're so many years past 2049, it gives you enough space to really carve out your own identity.".

In a recent development, impressively, Luisa looked to Villeneuve's 2017 movie to figure out the ideal way to do just that. "What was so fantastic about what Denis did with '2049' was, he didn't just rehash what Ridley had done," the showrunner told me. "He really created his own take on 'Blade Runner' that is very much his aesthetic. But it still felt like an evolution of Ridley's conversation." In effect, the key was to thread that very tricky needle for "2099.".

When it comes to the recent trend of legacy sequels that have dominated the last decade or so of franchise filmmaking, it can certainly feel like we can count the worthwhile ones on just one or two hands. Fortunately, for Silka Luisa and her creative team on "Blade Runner 2099," Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049" is basically the poster child for legacy sequels done right. Rather than simply retread all the same ground as before (looking at you, "Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens"), "Blade Runner 2049" moved the story forward and took some seriously substantial risks along the way.

According to Luisa, this gave her all the permission she needed to follow in its footsteps and take things in bold upcoming directions with her show. "That freed us up in a lot of different ways, because it meant we weren't just beholden to repeating the same thing over and over again," she explains. One massive wrinkle in the Prime Video series is the fact "Blade Runner 2099" takes place after a Replicant uprising has shaken up the status quo, putting humans at the bottom of the food chain for once. It's a strange dynamic that our two main characters Olwen (the Replicant Blade Runner played by Michelle Yeoh) and Cora (the human posing as a Replicant played by Hunter Schafer) are forced to navigate throughout the season.

As fans tune in, they can rest assured in the knowledge that the series is taking its cues from one of the most ambitious and boundary-pushing legacy sequels of them all. You could do a lot worse than that. All eight episodes of "Blade Runner 2099" are now on Prime Video.

When discussing the best Batman, I'm pretty sure many people will say that Michael Keaton is #1, and I'm not going to disagree. Keaton OWNED that role. That said, is he the most interesting live-action version of the character? I'm going to say no.

In fact, I'm one of those weirdos who will acknowledge that while The Dark Knight is most people's favorite Batman movie, I'm actually of the opinion that Matt Reeves’ The Batman is the best Batman flick. That's all because of Robert Pattinson, who I think is the most fascinating version of Batman yet.

With confirmation that Pattinson is the new James Bond, I have a good feeling that he might also be the most interesting version of 007 yet. Here's why.

According to recent reports, while many people will likely say that Keaton is the best Batman, I think it's even more likely that most people will say that Sean Connery is the best Bond. Every subsequent Bond actor has unfortunately been judged against Connery, with many people saying that they liked Daniel Craig's bruiser Bond since he was a callback to the tough guy Bond that Connery represented.

According to recent reports, connery is also the reason why some people disregard Roger Moore's Bond, as some people think he verges too far into the silly territory. Personally, of all men who have played Bond, my favorite is Pierce Brosnan, but I respect those who prefer George Lazenby or Timothy Dalton.

That remarked, I think Robert Pattinson, who I've already gone on record calling my favorite modern actor, will probably provide the most interesting take on the character yet. When trying to envision him as Bond, I think of his roles in Tenet, The Batman, and Primetime, all rolled into one. I see him being a subtler, quieter Bond than others (maybe closest to Dalton), and I'm looking forward to him creating his own version far removed from anything like Connery. Can you tell that I'm excited?

We've had a James Bond who's been Remington Steele, a James Bond who was in The Golden Compass, a James Bond who was Indiana Jones’ dad, and a James Bond who was in Flash Gordon, but we've never had a James Bond who was ALSO Batman, and I just love that this is now going to be a reality.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I know I'm not the only person who's ever wondered who has the better gadgets, or who would win in a fight, and now that same actor is literally going to be both characters. We're undoubtedly going to have people who are going to argue that Pattinson is a great Batman, but a terrible Bond, or a phenomenal Bond, but a terrible Batman.

Recent findings suggest that or, you'll have people like me who think that Pattinson is an excellent Batman and (hopefully!) an excellent Bond, and I love that we now live in a timeline where this is a thing. Stupendous!

Sources indicate that honestly, I feel like the search for the next Bond took FOREVER. In fact, just last year, I wrote about how I thought Aaron Pierre would make for a great Bond. Even though it took seemingly a million years to pick another 007, I feel like the final decision came out of nowhere.

Granted, Pattinson had been in the discussion to play Bond for some time now, but I feel like this reveal came out of the blue (Leave it to me to just learn that Pattinson has been manifesting this role for years).

Industry observers note that however, now that Pattinson has been confirmed, I'm actually now EXTREMELY excited for this new Bond movie. So much so that while I wasn't really interested before, I'm now all in for a new Bond film. So, great decision! Robert Pattinson can do no wrong!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that kerry Kennedy is not in Milan on political business, but it’s hard to rein in the enthusiasm of some Americans following the 2026 midterm elections. Democrats won decisive majorities in both the House and Senate, along with 24 of the 36 governors elections held this month. It was a blue tsunami. Kennedy—a lawyer and human rights activist born in 1959 to dynasty Democrats Robert and Ethel Kennedy—is in a celebratory mood.

She’s in town for one night only to attend a charity dinner in support of her foundation, the Robert & Ethel Kennedy Human Rights Center. But first she sits down with Vanity Fair Italia, and over the course of our chat, she takes her beloved poodle, Scamper, for a short walk; sips two cappuccinos (strictly decaf), one of them iced (she apologizes to the Italians present); eats some gianduiotti chocolates; gestures animatedly; and smooths her very blonde hair.

But above all, she never stops smiling: “In America you can only go so far in the attempt to avoid the rule of law and erode democracy,” she says, making clear that her political statements are delivered in her personal capacity, “because at a certain point, even if you’re the most powerful and the richest man there, democracy will bring you down. [The president] made a mess all over the world, but in the end, in America, democracy was stronger.”.

From left: Robert Kennedy Jr., Joseph P Kennedy Jr., Tory Kennedy, and Kerry Kennedy on January 1, 1994.

Vanity Fair: What do voters want today?Kerry Kennedy: They’re upset about high prices. And they don’t like the corruption.

What do you think will happen to Donald Trump and his associates?I think that [Representative] Jamie Raskin is now going to be the head of the Judiciary Committee. I happen to know him very, very, very well because Jamie and I studied for the bar together. He’s brilliant, he’s determined, and he hates anything that harms our Constitution. I think that Trump is going to face impeachment. The rumors are that Trump’s going to fire [Pete] Hegseth, but if he isn’t fired, he’ll certainly be impeached.

According to recent reports, what will be the repercussions of the blue tsunami for Tehran?Iran’s leader at the moment, [Mojtaba Khamenei], has seen his father murdered by Trump. His head of state was murdered by Trump. His spiritual leader was murdered by Trump. Now Trump wants to make a peace deal with this guy. The only way to make progress is for the Iranians to think that it’s not Trump but someone else who’s negotiating.

And what about Ukraine?The fact that Donald Trump sold out Western values in Ukraine for a barrel of oil from a mad, thieving, murderous dictator in Russia shocked the American people and shocked people around the world. Congress has the power of the purse, and now it’s going to exercise that power. But….

Industry observers note that but?He’s still the president for two more years. We didn’t get the White House.

Ethel Kennedy and daughter Kerry Kennedy circa 1979.

Who is your ideal candidate for the 2028 presidential election?Anyone whose last name is Democrat.

It has been revealed that do you think [President Barack] Obama played a role in the Democrats’ success?Obama is beloved. The only person who’s beloved more is Michelle [Obama]. And when I watched his speeches, he was so clear and concise about the differences between the Republicans and the Democrats, with his moral authority and his joy.

In a recent development, you’ve talked about how your mother supported your father. Can you share an example of that?My father was working for the Senate, and he was investigating organized crime’s infiltration of the Teamsters union, stealing pension funds from the rank-and-file Teamsters. There was a journalist from the New York Post who was also investigating, and somebody threw acid in his face. He was permanently blinded. A few days later, my mother got an anonymous letter saying, “Your children will be next.” She took her three oldest kids, put them in the back of her car, drove them to the Capitol, walked into the hearing room, and sat in the front row while daddy was interrogating Jimmy Hoffa, the head of the Teamsters.

It has been revealed that she was saying, “You’re not going to get to me through my children, and you’re not going to get to my husband through me. We are a fortress and we’re coming after you.” I don’t know how she grappled with the trauma.

She probably did it for her children.She needed to be there for us. She was an athlete. And if you feel physically mighty, it’s very helpful when you have to also be psychologically mighty. She would get up and go swimming, then horseback riding, sailing, and after a sail, she would go for a swim. She also had a very deep faith. She went to Mass every day, prayed before and after every meal, and she made us read the Bible out loud at the dinner table every night.

According to recent reports, are you that devout too? Yes. In December, I’ll step down from being president of this organization. I’ll stay on the board and I’ll be president emeritus and I’ll still be involved, but I want to go to divinity school.

Stephen Colbert and Kerry Kennedy on December 11, 2013.

At what university?I don’t know. I have to apply and be accepted.

In 2008 you wrote the bestseller Being Catholic Now. What does it mean to be Catholic in 2026?For Americans, we have had this extremely disruptive, terrifying time for the last two years, and there are existential threats that everybody in the world is facing. And suddenly there’s an American pope who’s saying, “When you feel this is wrong, it is wrong. When this president is allowing ICE agents to go into American cities and start shooting people, that’s wrong. We need to have compassion toward one another. We need to have love toward one another. Every human being is valuable.”.

In a recent development, he’s one of the few voices—not one Republican senator has stood up, and other leaders around the world really have not stood up. Mark Carney did from Canada.

Pedro Sánchez [Spain’s prime minister] did a little bit.Yes, but not much. The pope has been the main person, and I think that’s renewed people’s faith because it’s very simple as a political leader to call on people’s anger and hatred and fury. It’s a simple trick to get elected. But what people really want you to do in the end is call upon their better angels and say, “You’re good. I see that the God in me sees the God in you.” That is the alternative message, and that’s the spiritual message. I think that it’s created a revival of faith. My daughter Cara is 31 years old, and every Sunday night, she and all of her friends go to church and it’s packed.

What lesson did you learn from your parents?When we were kids, when we would have a battle, and there were lots of battles, my father always did the same thing. He would bring two of us into a room. My brother had to be silent, and I would tell my father what happened and all the horrible things my brother did. And then I’d have to be silent, and he would tell his story. And then it would be clear that neither of us was completely innocent. We would have to kiss and make up and go to our rooms to read for an hour. His message to us was his message to our country, which is: You have to stop thinking of your adversary as your enemy and think of them as your brother and sister.

Your brother, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., right now the secretary of health in the Trump administration, is known for his anti-vax views. You’ve often said, “I love him very much, but I don’t agree with him.”We were very close, but he changed and went way over there. And that’s where he is today. But we have much more in common than not.

Robert F. Kennedy Jr and Kerry Kennedy on May 20, 2015.

Do you discuss politics today?I’m not going to go talk to him about vaccine policy. That’s not going to change him, and he’s not going to change me. So when I’m with him, I want to talk about, how are his animals? How are his children? His daughter, who is my goddaughter, Kyra, lives here in Milan, and she’s getting married to an Italian, and I’m so happy for her. There are many things to talk about besides vaccines.

Your shared past also includes the assassination of your father. Who told you that news?We were all together in the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles and we were watching the returns, but I was eight and I went to sleep. I woke up very early the next morning because I was still on East Coast time, and I went into the living room area of my hotel room. I turned on the TV to watch Bugs Bunny. That’s how I learned.

Sources indicate that did you guys see a therapist when you were little?Of course not. It was 1968. If it happened today, every kid would get their own therapist; back then, you dealt with it.

And how did you deal with it?Terribly.

Really?Other students were reading Charlotte’s Web, and I was trying to figure out if somebody was going to kill someone in my family. What happens if Mommy dies? Are they going to split us up? Who could take 11 kids? Houses aren’t big. Where do we go? Would we see each other on Christmas?

Were you a happy little girl before that day?When I was a child, my parents really didn’t separate my father’s life and work from our home. So Daddy would call my mother and say, “You know what? There are three or four of us. We’re trying to work out this [policy] issue. Could we come home for lunch?” Sure. And then he’d call back half an hour later. “Actually, now we’re 12.”.

Sources indicate that they sat at the dining room table, and there would be three or four kids doing homework and eating peanut butter and jelly sandwiches and asking them to pass the milk. And then they would be talking about these issues. My mother would come in and say, “Time to play football.” And everybody would get up and go out. For us kids, it felt like we were part of something bigger.

In a recent development, your latest book, which has just been published, is a biography of your mother: Ethel Kennedy: The Extraordinary Life and Bold Legacy. What kind of person was she?My mother loved men. If you’re a woman, you’re great, and you’re her friend. But when a man was watching, it was incredible. Her whole life, that’s the way she was. When she was 96 and her mind was kind of in and out, I called her from my hotel in Milan and I noted, “I’m here. Can I bring you anything? Do you want some limoncello or a bag of that beautiful spaghetti that they sell at the airport? What can I bring you from Italy?” And she answered, “An Italian boyfriend would be nice.”.

#200339. Tech Report: 10 Years Later, Netflix's $120 Million Flop Deserves a Season 2

Tech Report: 10 Years Later, Netflix's $120 Million Flop Deserves a Season 2

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1275 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Polygon

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that in 2016, Netflix was riding high.
  • It has been revealed that this Turkey Day, as Polygon celebrates our favorite failures and flops from the world of entertainment, it's time to resurrect a Netflix original that earned (mostly) rave reviews but got canceled after just one season for what, in hindsight, feels like an easily avoidable reason.
  • Created by Baz Luhrmann (Moulin Rouge, The Great Gatsby, Romeo + Juliet) and playwright Stephen Adly Guirgis, The Get Down traces the origin story of hip-hop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in 2016, Netflix was riding high. The shift to original programming, which had kicked off three years earlier with House of Cards, was now proving to be an undeniable success. That year marked the return of hit indicates like Daredevil, Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt, BoJack Horseman, and Orange is the New Black, along with the debut of brand-defining series Stranger Things and The Crown. All of these shows have remained in the cultural zeitgeist, but arguably the best original series released on Netflix in 2016 has all but disappeared from the conversation.

It has been revealed that this Turkey Day, as Polygon celebrates our favorite failures and flops from the world of entertainment, it's time to resurrect a Netflix original that earned (mostly) rave reviews but got canceled after just one season for what, in hindsight, feels like an easily avoidable reason. Not only is The Get Down an overlooked masterpiece, but 10 years later, it's due for a revival.

Created by Baz Luhrmann (Moulin Rouge, The Great Gatsby, Romeo + Juliet) and playwright Stephen Adly Guirgis, The Get Down traces the origin story of hip-hop. Deep within the Bronx, MCs hype local crowds with rhythmic lyricism performed over percussive instrumental breaks pulled by pioneering DJs from funk, soul, and disco records. The series centers on one such MC, Zeke "Books" Figuero (Justice Smith), and his DJ, Curtis "Shaolin Fantastic" Caldwell (Shameik Moore), as they stumble into a newly introduced art form.

While much of the story follows these two young Black men as they hustle and struggle to succeed, The Get Down's scope is even grander. It's the story of Upcoming York City in the 1970s and everything that entails, from corrupt politicians and gangsters to the rising punk music scene in Manhattan. Disco defines the series almost as much as hip-hop, with female protagonist Mylene Cruz (Herizen F. Guardiola) representing the power of the then-dominant genre as a beautiful woman with an incredible voice who's stuck singing in church when she wants to be a radio star.

The absolutely stacked cast also includes Yahya Abdul-Mateen II as gangster disco prince Clarence "Cadillac" Caldwell, Jimmy Smits as a local political boss, Giancarlo Esposito as Mylene's pastor father, Mamoudou Athie as real-life DJ legend Grandmaster Flash, and Daveed Diggs as adult Ezekiel narrating the story (with hip-hop icon Nas providing his dubbed-in rapping voice). It's an all-star team-up firing on all cylinders.

According to recent reports, the Get Down has all the usual flourishes of a Luhrmann production. It's a beautifully realized world that glitters in the neon lights of Upcoming York without attempting to hide the crime and decay that defined the city in the 1970s. Telling a story about hip-hop and disco also allows Luhrmann to fill the show with elevated musical moments that are on par with the best scenes from Moulin Rouge, while also feeling far more grounded. This isn't a musical in the sense that characters don't spontaneously break into song to move the plot forward or express their emotions, but it still manages to achieve a similarly staggering effect each time a record spins and an MC picks up the mic.

Industry observers note that it's also deeply reverent toward the history of hip-hop. Music icons Nas, Grandmaster Flash, and Kurtis Blow organized a hip-hop boot camp to teach the young cast about the art form. In an interview with Mother Jones, Grandmaster Flash praised the series for demystifying the earliest origins of the genre he helped create.

According to recent reports, "Hip-hop has always been chronologically misunderstood," he said. "Too many times, people are hearing the story from the second floor. Nobody’s heard the story from the basement. If hip-hop was a cake, all I can tell you is the eggs, the flour, the sugar, the vanilla — the ingredient years. This is what Baz wanted to put on film.".

Meanwhile, Nas, who arrived in the '90s and redefined rap music with his vibrant descriptions of life in the Brooklyn projects, conveyed through naturalistic lyrical poetry, wrote every single bar delivered by Ezekiel on the show.

"I am Ezekiel," he told Rolling Stone. "Ezekiel is older than me, but I am that.".

Recent findings suggest that in other words, The Get Down wasn't just Luhrmann's retelling of a famous story. It was a deeply researched, loving tribute to the creation of hip-hop, told by the people who defined the genre from the very start.

The Get Down dropped six episodes on Netflix in August 2016, with another five released in April 2017 to complete the first season. The second batch picks up a year later in the story as well, with Mylene's singing career taking off while Ezekiel struggles to keep up, weighed down by the world he grew up in.

The show was canceled soon afterward for a variety of reasons, including its astronomical cost. In an article breaking down the rise and fall of The Get Down, IndieWire called it "the best $120 million Netflix has ever spent.".

Ultimately, the show's downfall reportedly traces back to Luhrmann. While the director took a hands-on approach in crafting season 1 (even directing the pilot episode himself), he decided to take a step back with season 2 to return to film and make Elvis. This didn't mean the show had to stop, though. In a sense, that approach had pretty much defined the entire series from day one.

It has been revealed that “Because I come from community storytelling, you have to get the community’s trust,” Luhrmann told IndieWire. “So I started to reach out to the people whose story it was, because it’s not my story. I feel like I just curated that story.”.

Recent findings suggest that but Netflix balked, and The Get Down came to a disappointingly early end. In a sense, it was a sign of things to come. In the years since, the streamer has developed an unfortunate reputation for canceling great shows too early and for relying on big-name talent over good storytelling and original ideas (although The Get Down had plenty of both).

In a recent development, A decade after its demise, the chances of a revival seem slim. There isn't exactly a devoted fanbase crying out for more, and Luhrmann is already busy working on his next movie. Then again, it's not totally impossible either. After all, The Get Down's core duo has only gotten more famous in the years since, with Shameik Moore voicing Miles Morales in the Spider-Verse movies and Justice Smith starring in everything from Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves to Now You See Me: Now You Don't. Maybe that's enough to entice some Netflix executive.

In a recent development, A follow-up could reunite Smith and Moore (and the rest of the cast) and pick up their story a decade later. The late '80s was a golden age for hip-hop, with artists like Eric B. & Rakim, Significant Daddy Kane, LL Cool J, Public Enemy, and N.W.A dominating the airwaves on both sides of the country. A newly introduced season of The Get Down could explore what happens when an art form born out of the Bronx projects goes mainstream — and how that kind of explosive success can often leave the original creators behind.

It has been revealed that is it a long shot​​​​​​​? Of course, but either way, The Get Down remains a shining example of what's starting to feel like the long-gone golden age of Netflix programming. So why not give it a spin? And maybe if enough people do, we'll finally get a season 2.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday isn't until Nov. 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sales have been ramping up for several days. For frequent Amazon shoppers, Prime can rapidly pay for itself—mostly thanks to the free shipping perk. But how does the math shake out if you aren't regularly ordering from Amazon? Is it worth signing up if you only shop during major sales?

According to recent reports, millions of Amazon Prime customers right now pay $14.99 per month or $139 per year for their memberships—though other plans cost less if you qualify. For example, the Amazon Prime Student program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

If you’re on the fence about signing up for (or renewing) your Prime membership, here’s how to judge whether or not the benefits outweigh the $139 cost.

Here are the main perks of Amazon Prime that make it worth the cost for so many people.

Sources indicate that free two-day shipping on millions of items: This is the main draw of Prime. If you shop frequently on Amazon and want quick free delivery, the shipping perks alone may make Prime worthwhile. Prime members also get free same-day delivery on over 3 million items in eligible areas. The ultra-fast (and morally suspect) shipping usually costs $9.99 per order for non-members, though you can choose lower-cost or free shipping options if you're willing to place larger orders and wait longer to receive them.

It has been revealed that access to Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals. If you ask me, the content library isn’t as robust as Netflix or Hulu, but this is still an added value.

Other Prime benefits: You also get Amazon Music for streaming songs, Prime Reading for ebooks, magazines, and audiobooks; Prime gaming, free photo storage, and occasional exclusive discounts/deals.

Sources indicate that amazon Prime Rewards Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon/Whole Foods purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the annual fee.

It has been revealed that number of people: Prime benefits can be shared with other members of your household. The more users, the more value per person.

Let's say you don't care about Prime Video, Amazon Music, or free e-books, and just want to know if you'll save money you would otherwise be spending on shipping.

Industry observers note that for non-Prime members, Amazon requires a minimum order of $35 to qualify for free shipping on eligible items. The average shipping costs for non-members aren't publicly listed, and can vary by item and shipping speed, typically ranging from $5 to $10.

For our purposes, I messed around on my non-shared, non-Prime Amazon account to find an average shipping cost of around $6 per order (assuming the order total fell below the $35 threshold, of course). Of course, shipping costs will vary depending on the item and how quickly you want it, but let’s compare the cost to the appeal of Prime’s two-day shipping option. So, we have the cost of individual online orders (around six bucks) compared to the free delivery that comes with an $139 annual fee. This means the costs you’d save on shipping alone make Prime worth the cost as long as you place more than two dozen orders in a year.

In other words: The $139 annual fee pays for itself as long as you order from Amazon Prime at least twice a month.

Sources indicate that of course, this conclusion is strictly in terms of shipping costs. How it stacks up ethically is between you and the person in the mirror.

Sources indicate that and then there's this vital caveat: You can still get free shipping from Amazon without a Prime membership, provided your order has $35 or more of eligible items. However, this won't grant you Prime shipping speed—your order will typically take five to eight days to be delivered. But you can place fewer, larger orders and wait a little longer, and still never pay for shipping.

Also worth considering is how much of that membership cost you'll be able to recoup via exclusive Prime Day offers. During the sale, some items will be heavily discounted only for Prime members—but whether the Prime Day price is really a "deal" will vary greatly based on the item you're buying. Some of those "significant discounts" aren't any greater than what the item typically sells for. The Prime Day price can even be higher than other sale prices throughout the year. That's why it's important to make sure what you're ordering is something you planned to buy anyway—and that the sale price is actually a true bargain—before you order.

The cost of a Prime membership is a solid value for anyone using Amazon 23 times per year or more—especially if you're also watching shows on Prime Video or purchasing something that is deeply discounted for Prime Day. But if you only shop on Amazon a few times a year and don't take advantage of Prime Day offers or the other benefits, then that $139 annual fee isn't necessarily paying for itself.

According to recent reports, yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quentin Tarantino has returned to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" with "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" (why not read our review of the upcoming movie here?). But this time, while Tarantino penned the script, he isn't in the director's chair. Instead, he's handed directing duties over to his pal David Fincher (who is ending his exclusive deal with Netflix with the film). Tarantino might not be behind the camera, but he still has a presence in the film, and it echoes something he did in "Hollywood" as well.

Industry observers note that early in "Cliff Booth," we're introduced to Charlie Peters, a hot-tempered TV star played by Scott Caan. To speed-run us through Charlie's successful career, we're given a little montage of his various roles, and that montage is narrated by none other than Tarantino, whose very recognizable voice provides some humorous details about Charlie's work.

Recent findings suggest that fans of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" will recall that Tarantino also provided narration in that movie, too. He actually wasn't the only narrator, either, because during one scene, Kurt Russell, who plays a stuntman named Randy in that film, also provides a little narration. As for Tarantino, he also voiced some crucial narration during a pivotal scene in "The Hateful Eight.".

In fact, the filmmaker has a history of popping up in his movies, either via a voice cameo or a physical appearance. He has a pretty significant role in "Reservoir Dogs," makes a memorable cameo in "Pulp Fiction," gets to use an abysmal Australian accent in "Django Unchained," has his voice heard during a movie playing in "Inglourious Basterds" (and also plays a corpse in the film), plays a bartender in "Death Proof," portrays one of the members of the Crazy 88 gang in "Kill Bill," and lends his voice to an answering machine in "Jackie Brown.".

So while "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" may not technically be a Quentin Tarantino movie, it still feels like one, right down to the obligatory cameo.

21 Best Thanksgiving Movies to Stream This Week

📅 24 Nov 2021 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2103 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that sandwiched between the kitschy horrors of Halloween and the commercialized merriment of Christmas, Thanksgiving is often unfairly overlooked as a cinematic main course.
  • Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, we’ve collected 21 Thanksgiving movies (and Thanksgiving-adjacent movies) that capture the spirit of the holiday—turkey-trotting, tossing the pigskin, carb-loading, fighting with your family, and then overheating in a gorgeous cashmere sweater.
  • This isn’t known as the quintessential Thanksgiving movie for nothing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sandwiched between the kitschy horrors of Halloween and the commercialized merriment of Christmas, Thanksgiving is often unfairly overlooked as a cinematic main course. But while there might not be a feast’s worth of Thanksgiving movies, there is undoubtedly an appetite for Thanksgiving fare in film. Look no further than the inclusion of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in Miracle on 34th Street or Wednesday Adams’s sinister (if historically-accurate) re-enactment in Addams Family Values for proof that audiences love turkey’s least favorite holiday. Of course, Thanksgiving tends to get a better treatment on TV, inspiring canonical episodes of Gossip Girl, Friends, Master of None, and, of course, A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving.

Recent findings suggest that nevertheless, we’ve collected 21 Thanksgiving movies (and Thanksgiving-adjacent movies) that capture the spirit of the holiday—turkey-trotting, tossing the pigskin, carb-loading, fighting with your family, and then overheating in a gorgeous cashmere sweater. Here’s to finding post-meal common ground with one of the titles on this list.

This isn’t known as the quintessential Thanksgiving movie for nothing. You know the story: Steve Martin’s uptight marketing executive, Neal, just wants to travel from Upcoming York to Chicago for turkey with his family. His plans for an uneventful trip are foiled again and again by John Candy’s boisterous shower-ring salesman, Del, who’s eager to make friends with Neal during their wayward journey. We will never look at pillows—or rental car agents—the same way again.

Don’t let the word Christmas in the title scare you away. This 2016 ensemble comedy starring Danny Glover, Kimberly Elise, Mo’Nique, and Gabrielle Union has undeniable Thanksgiving vibes. Produced by Will Packer and originally sold to Universal Pictures under the title A Meyers Thanksgiving, Almost Christmas follows the dysfunctional Meyers family as the family patriarch, Walter Meyers (Glover), tries to get through his first holiday season after the death of his wife. While it isn’t exactly about Thanksgiving per se, most of the best moments in Almost Christmas—including Elise chasing Romany Malco away from the table with a shotgun, or the whole table having to pretend to like Mo’Nique’s terrible food—take place during large family gatherings around the dinner table. What could be more Thanksgiving-coded than that? With an all-star cast of Black actors that also includes J.B. Smoove, Nicole Ari Parker, Omar Epps, and Gladys Knight, Almost Christmas feels like a homecoming full of your favorite uncles and aunties. And, to be fair, isn’t Thanksgiving almost Christmas?

The turkey isn’t the only thing getting carved up in this holiday slasher. Starring Patrick Dempsey and Tik Toker turned recording artist turned film actress Addison Rae, Thanksgiving begins with a Black Friday sale gone horribly awry in Plymouth, Massachusetts, leading to the death of multiple customers. The following year, a murderous slasher wearing a John Carver mask is wreaking havoc in Plymouth, and targeting Rae’s Gaby and her friends. If you’re not feeling warm and gooey on over the holiday, you might want to throw on Thanksgiving and watch Rae and Dempsey’s Sheriff Eric Newton try and track down and escape the clutches of a grisly murderer.

In Jodie Foster’s comedy, Holly Hunter plays Claudia Larson, who returns home for Thanksgiving after losing her job and learning that her daughter (My So-Called Life–era Claire Danes) looks to spend the holiday with a boyfriend. The family she returns to is filled with colorful performances from Anne Bancroft and Charles Durning as her eclectic parents, Robert Downey Jr. as her misanthrope brother, and Dylan McDermott as a semi-mysterious dinner guest.

Fantastic Mr. Fox isn’t technically about Thanksgiving, or even really about humans. And yet, Wes Anderson’s 2009 stop-motion film, featuring the voices of George Clooney and Meryl Streep, has been labeled a Thanksgiving must-watch. Perhaps that’s because the film, based on Roald Dahl’s classic children’s novel, is all about animals trying to escape the tyranny of farmers—something every turkey not lucky enough to be pardoned by the president wishes it could do around Thanksgiving time. Beyond the war between animals and farmers, Anderson’s rustic color palette filled with burnt orange—and the massive feast that brings a diverse array of animals around a dinner table after they successfully joined forces to steal food from their nemeses—are full of the spirit of Thanksgiving.

Industry observers note that at times, the titular April’s (Katie Holmes) fate feels as if it rests on whether she’ll successfully cook a turkey in her crowded Lower East Side apartment. As April prepares to host her suburban Pennsylvania family, the high-stakes nature of spending a day hunkered down with relatives—played by Patricia Clarkson, Oliver Platt, Alison Pill, and John Gallagher Jr.—rushes in.

Sometimes getting families together over the holidays is fraught. In this 1997 moody drama directed by Ang Lee, two affluent Connecticut families unravel over Thanksgiving break as their secrets come to lights. The ensemble cast includes stalwart actors Kevin Kline, Joan Allen, Sigourney Weaver as messy parents, and, at that point, up and comers, Tobey Maguire, Elijah Wood, and Christina Ricci as their even more troubled teens. The Ice Storm, which won best screenplay at Cannes Film Festival, is rife with adultery, substance abuse, as well as surprising turns from a host of talented actors and a sharp early film from one of cinema’s most celebrated directors.

In a recent development, nothing feels more nostalgic during Thanksgiving than watching Snoopy whip up a makeshift meal with jelly beans, popcorn, and mountains of buttered toast for all of his Peanuts pals. And Vince Guraldi’s timeless score makes for a perfect soundtrack to your own festivities.

Industry observers note that A Thanksgiving flashback provides key context for the complicated dynamics amongst this group of recently-reunited college friends, played by Glenn Close, Kevin Kline, Jeff Goldblum, Mary Kay Place, and William Hurt. Lawrence Kasdan’s film earned three Oscar nominations, including best picture, original screenplay, and supporting actress for Close.

While not a Thanksgiving-themed film, protagonist Nola Darling (Tracy Camilla Johns) invites all three of her potential suitors to a tense dinner on that very holiday, making her memorable decision between them from her head-of-the-table vantage point. This was most of the world’s introduction to Spike Lee, both as an actor and director, and the electricity is still palpable. And if you’ve gotta have more? You can always stream the 2017 Netflix original series of the same name, starring Lee and DeWanda Wise as Nola Darling.

It has been revealed that rian Johnson’s whodunnit has all the trappings of a Thanksgiving movie, without ever mentioning the holiday. There’s family infighting, Chris Evans in a cable-knit sweater, foggy fall weather, and even a political allegory about the treatment of people of color. Also not about Thanksgiving, but worthy viewing for the full family: Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery, which hit theaters last November.

In a recent development, the same year that Merriam-Webster acknowledged Instagram captions everywhere by adding “Friendsgiving” to the dictionary, a movie of the same name was released. True to its titular tradition, a group of friends convenes for a meal that inevitably devolves into chaos.

Recent findings suggest that while not an outright Thanksgiving movie, 1997’s ensemble dramedy contains some of the most sumptuous shots of food ever committed to film. After the death of their family matriarch, a group of disparate relatives must put aside their differences and reconvene for a weekly Sunday dinner. Starring Vivica A. Fox, Vanessa Williams, and Nia Long, Soul Food captures the bonding powers that plates of cornbread, catfish, and collard greens can bring.

Sources indicate that this 1976 best picture Oscar winner stars Sylvester Stallone as the eponymous down-on-his-luck boxer, whose fate begins to change with the meeting of his future wife, Adrian (Talia Shire). “To you, it’s Thanksgiving. To me, it’s Thursday,” Rocky tells Adrian as he whisks her away from a disastrous family feast minutes after her brother Paulie (Burt Young) hurls her turkey into the nearby alley. As fans of the franchise, which has debuted several films over the Thanksgiving holiday, know, their Thanksgiving meet-cute will stand the test of time.

Industry observers note that thanksgiving isn’t always about bickering with your blood relatives. Spend Thanksgiving with Instant Family, which stars Mark Wahlberg and Rose Byrne as Pete and Ellie Wagner, an unwitting couple who, overnight, become parents to three foster children. Their decision to become parents happens over  a tense Thanksgiving dinner where Ellie’s family shares they don’t think that Pete and Ellie were ever really cut out to be parents. In an effort to prove them wrong, the Wagners wind up biting off more than they bargained for as they become foster parents to three children, the eldest played by Madame Web star Isabela Merced.

Sources indicate that before Greta Gerwig forced Noah Baumbach to write Barbie with her, there was Mistress America. Written by the real-life couple who helmed the billion dollar blockbuster, this 2015 Sundance favorite centers on the unlikely friendship between Lola Kirke’s Tracy, a first-year college student alone in Fresh York, and Gerwig’s Brooke, the Times Square-living twentysomething who will soon become her stepsister. Conflict between the pair gets resolved on Thanksgiving at New York City’s Veselka, a Ukrainian institution where pierogis stand in for the traditional bird.

Recent findings suggest that greta Gerwig must really love Thanksgiving. The auteur’s Oscar-nominated take on the Louisa May Alcott classic is brimming with cozy, Thanksgiving-esque vibes. Set largely in the weeks before Christmas, the March sisters (Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Eliza Scanlen, and Florence Pugh) and matriarch (Laura Dern) battle wits, trot through the snow, and stage living room plays in a film that feels reminiscent of many a-family gatherings.

“First, let’s give thanks to our families not being here. It’s always easier without the family,” Adam Sandler’s George Simmons, a stand-up comedian who has been newly diagnosed with cancer, states to a group of fresh friends. In Judd Apatow’s 2009 dramedy, George attempts to revamp his fledgling career in the eleventh hour with the help of aspiring comic Ira Wright (Seth Rogen). At one point, he  joins the younger talent’s friendsgiving festivities, where the table is surrounded by stars including Jonah Hill, Jason Schwartzman, Aubrey Plaza, and Bo Burnham.

In one of the newer entries to the turkey day canon, Stephen Karam adapts his 2015 Pulitzer finalist play of the same name, exploring the long-held resentments and deeply-rooted admiration that live in an East Coast family. Jayne Houdyshell reprises her Tony-winning role as Deirdre alongside a stacked ensemble, including Richard Jenkins, June Squibb, Beanie Feldstein, Steven Yeun, and Amy Schumer, all gathered in a drab Chinatown apartment for Thanksgiving.

Prisoners finds Hugh Jackman and Jake Gyllenhaal teaming up to find a pair of missing girls who were abducted after Thanksgiving dinner in Conyers, Pennsylvania. EGOT recipient Viola Davis also stars in the thriller as the mother of one of the kidnapped girls. Directed by Dune’s Denis Villeneuve, Prisoners is an unconventional and unsettling Thanksgiving film.

Another unconventional choice, Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man is arguably the only superhero movie that doubles as a Thanksgiving movie. While the central action follows Tobey Maguire’s Peter Parker, there’s a pivotal scene set at Thanksgiving dinner that directly follows a heated battle between Spider-Man and the Green Goblin (a.k.a Norman Osborne, played by Willem Dafoe.) Parker and Osborne have Thanksgiving dinner together with MJ (Kirsten Dunst), Harry Osborne (James Franco), and Aunt May (Rosemary Harris). During the meal, Osborne comes to the stunning realization that Peter Parker is, in fact, Spider-Man. Others have already made the case that the first Spider-Man film deserves to be included in the Thanksgiving canon. The way Dafoe carves the turkey is also both sinister and iconic, as is Maguire apologizing for his tardiness because he “had to beat an old lady with a stick to get these cranberries.”.

#200334. Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (813 w)

Where Are Rick Dalton and Sharon Tate in ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (813 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Indiewire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
