💡 Key Takeaways
  • “I’m not one of those people that try to act like I don’t want the thing.
  • In a recent development, though her 2023 role in “The Color Purple” cemented the Grammy winner’s status as a performer who has at the very least been nominated for each letter of EGOT, the real reward the recognition among her peers has brought is the opportunity to executive produce and star in projects like the Walter Thompson-Hernandez film “If I Go Will They Miss Me,” which premiered at Sundance 2026 to rave reviews.
  • Sources indicate that the coming-of-age drama set in Watts, California sees the actress play a mother named Lozita doing her best to hold her family together while there’s inscrutable tension between her partner, recently released from prison, and their imaginative 12-year-old son.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“I’m not one of those people that try to act like I don’t want the thing. I want the thing. I’m excited about the thing,” remarked recent Academy Award nominee Danielle Brooks. “I know how much it has impacted little Dani when I’ve watched Oprah Winfrey or Whoopi Goldberg or Viola Davis or Halle Berry receive [Oscars], and listened even to the speeches now, [from Emmy winners] Niecy Nash-Betts and Sheryl Lee Ralph. They push you to continue to work hard.”.

In a recent development, though her 2023 role in “The Color Purple” cemented the Grammy winner’s status as a performer who has at the very least been nominated for each letter of EGOT, the real reward the recognition among her peers has brought is the opportunity to executive produce and star in projects like the Walter Thompson-Hernandez film “If I Go Will They Miss Me,” which premiered at Sundance 2026 to rave reviews. “Yes, I have the desire to be receiving awards one day,” mentioned Brooks, “but at the end of the day, I get to do that with my work. I get to do that with stories like ‘If I Go,’ where my goal is for people to feel seen.” Related Stories What Are Local Movie Theaters Showing for Thanksgiving 2026? ‘All of a Sudden’: Why Does an 11-Minute Scene Centered on a Whiteboard Lecture Work So Well Onscreen?

Sources indicate that the coming-of-age drama set in Watts, California sees the actress play a mother named Lozita doing her best to hold her family together while there’s inscrutable tension between her partner, recently released from prison, and their imaginative 12-year-old son. “I started out in theater, so to me, it’s never been about a paycheck,” joked Brooks. “It’s always been about the story and what you’re putting out into the world. And so, when I watched [Thompson-Hernandez’s] short, I was like, ‘Yo, this is different. I ain’t never seen nothing like this.’ And it was captivating just the way he was shooting it.”.

Expanding on what drew her to the project, which came to her during her time bouncing between Los Angeles awards press for “The Color Purple,” and the Upcoming Zealand set of “A Minecraft Movie,” Brooks said “They handed me the script and it was really the conversation, sitting down with Walter, his passion for his community, hearing about the real Lozita who had unfortunately passed away from cancer two years prior, hearing about the Compton Cowboys, just getting to talk to him about relationships between kids and their parents and the complications that it can bring.”.

According to recent reports, she remarked, “I like the balance. I got to have a little comedy, but I got to do some drama and it does my heart well.” While “Minecraft” brought her “laughs all day with Jack Black and Jason Momoa,” “If I Go” brought Brooks “purpose.” “I’m excited that we get to share stories like this where people are really dealing with their personal problems and healing and all of that stuff,” she said.

Having screened the film in Los Angeles the night before, Brooks said “You can feel the energy of everyone feeling super represented and feeling a sense of ownership. It’s cool hearing the audience be like, ‘Yeah, yeah,’ When you talk about the planes passing by, or the story about the fuel engines falling on elementary schools. People remember and know that to be a part of what has happened in LA, and the fabric of LA.”.

According to recent reports, one job that was foundational to how she approaches projects like “If I Go” happens to be Brooks’ breakout role as Taystee on “Orange Is the New Black.” Coming out of the prestigious Julliard School, her mind was more so on “how am I going to make my money for the subway and pay for my college tuition and how am I going to pay for this PB&J sandwich?,” when she booked the role on the series for the then-nascent streaming service Netflix. “I didn’t know what I was stepping into at the time. ‘Orange’ was looked at as a webseries, so nobody knew what this was about to be. But once we got into the work, I was like, ‘Oh, this is deeper than that.’ I remember talking to people who’ve been incarcerated, and I remember even doing a clothing drive for women who have just come out of prison so that they could have clothes for job interviews and stuff like that. We were really invested in the community and giving back,” mentioned Brooks.

Sources indicate that “We had that as a group, as storytellers, but then individually, I was watching my co-stars have a point of view, have something to say. And so, I [was] just learning that being an artist is also a form of activism,” she noted. “That was one of the beginning seeds planted in my head once I was in the industry, because I’ve always known that what we do is about service, that’s number one. But I hadn’t experienced that on this level.”.

Sources indicate that since then, Brooks’ goal has been to tell at least one story a year that incorporates a bit of activism, and with “If I Go,” the actress and producer has been more active than ever. “I’ve deemed us the little engine that could, because I really believe that we can take this far. My goal is that we just get as many eyeballs on it as we can. But the truth of the matter is nothing moves like money does. And that’s what I’ve learned is you’ve got to get really creative and strategic about how you can push a movie into the face of the people when you don’t have the money.”.

It has been revealed that “If I Go Will They Miss Me,” distributed by Rich Spirit, has truly been an indie success story, making over $1 million at the box office from the humblest of beginnings. As Brooks noted, that haul has been hard fought, with her, Thompson-Hernandez, and her co-star J. Alphonse Nicholson touring as much of the country as they can to screen the film, and even abroad. “I’m going to Africa this week, I got invited, but then I learned there’s a film festival in Africa. So, I’m like, ‘Can we take the film to Africa?’ And they said, ‘Yes.’ So now, the film’s going to be in the festival there,” said the actress.

It has been revealed that she continued, “It’s even in the form of fashion. People pay attention to what you’re wearing and then they’re like, ‘Why you got that on? Oh! She had a premiere.’ Boom. It’s insane how many tricks I have been working to get people to pay attention to this film that is worth paying attention to.”.

One of the more beautiful aspects of this “If I Go” experience has been the way in which her community has shown up for her and the film. Snoop Dogg and Ava DuVernay have Instagrammed about it, while Helen Hunt and André Holland have even hosted talk backs for the film. But in terms of creativity, one marketing strategy takes the cake. “Issa Rae, even at her restaurant, she did a menu dedicated to ‘If I Go’ where it was a discount, 15 percent off or something if you bought a ticket,” she stated. “People understand the importance of this,” said Brooks. “If the film wasn’t good, I wouldn’t be doing all this.”.

On the awards front, the challenge is still getting the film in front of the steak eaters who still make up a good chunk of the awards body, and maybe do not immediately think they identify with the material. “The Academy is working really hard to change that narrative by who is allowed to vote. The voting party is shifting, but that’s what I’m experiencing right now,” noted Brooks.

But regular filmgoers have a role in getting smaller, truly independent films awards recognition too. “The general audience plays a huge part because the culture tells the voters where to look, what is important,” said the actress. “The people, we have a voice in this too. I think we make it very clear what we want to see, but it’s a weird cycle.” Studio films have a budget for billboards, commercials, advertisements, and more. “When you are a small independent film, you have to be that big machine on your own to get it out there. And that’s a lot of work, and that’s a lot of time, and that’s a lot of smarts,” said Brooks. “You’ve got to have a lot of faith and hope too. You’ve just got to believe that what you’ve created is strong. And I do know that we all do, myself, J. Alphonse, Walter, MACRO, Rich Spirit, we believe in this film wholeheartedly.”.

“Movies like these are worth telling, and I think they do reach who they need to reach, and they do lock in with the world on a larger scale when they’re supposed to,” said Brooks, reflecting on the fruitful journey “If I Go” has already had so far. “This is the thing I’m most proud of in my whole career because just the fact that people are having conversations, hard conversations with their loved ones, and they’re finding ways to heal.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

[Editor’s Note: The following review contains spoilers for “The Lowdown” Season 2 Episode 8, “The Tower” — including the finale’s ending.].

Recent findings suggest that “I saw the structure of the episode as these kind of waves that crash upon Lee,” Ethan Hawke stated in an interview about “The Lowdown‘s” Season 2 finale. “The way life works, it’s not like, ‘Oh, this one thing happens and then you change.’ It’s usually a series of things that happen, and the walls of your defenses come down.”.

It has been revealed that lee’s walls were certainly up when “The Lowdown” Season 2 began. Untethered by the acclaim for his Season 1 exposé on Dale Washberg (Tim Blake Nelson), Lee reacts with vehement defensiveness. He mocks the journalists who named him Tulsa’s Journalist of the Year during his acceptance speech. He alienates his friends and embarrasses his daughter. Related Stories Danielle Brooks Shares Insights from the Indie Success of ‘If I Go Will They Miss Me’ Will Ferrell Golf Comedy ‘The Hawk’ Canceled at Netflix After Just One Season.

Recent findings suggest that he’s a mess, and when Ginger (Betty Gilpin) walks into his life with a tantalizing fresh story, he’s lucky — not because she’s the woman of his dreams carrying his drug of choice (a “truthstorian’s” next crusade), but because grounding forces are on the way in the form of his estranged father, Lee Raybon Sr. (Tommy Lee Jones), as well as a few clear-eyed, full-throated friends. Over the course of a riveting, revelatory Season 2, they all help to bring Lee back to himself, one wave at a time.

In a recent development, the finale’s first swell comes as quite a surprise — two surprises, really. When Lee pulls up to the funeral home, prepared to pay a terse goodbye to his departed dad, so, too, does his former business partner and best friend, Wendell (played by Peter Dinklage). Wendell tells Lee he’ll “always be grateful” for Senior’s guidance when they were younger, and it’s immediately clear he’s not about to take the man’s final tribute as lightly as his son may have hoped.

“When Tommy’s character dies and there’s a funeral, we’re all like, ‘Well, wouldn’t Wendell be there?’ I mean, they’re really great friends,'” Hawke mentioned. “I called Peter up and I was like, ‘Is there any way you’d come down for one day to be just at this funeral?’ And Peter was shooting in London and flew in and flew right back. He came in and made it happen for us.”.

Industry observers note that but Dinklage’s return was no mere cameo. Creator Sterlin Harjo knew better than to let the opportunity go to waste.

“I think there was a Shakespeare monologue in it first, and it was beautiful,” Harjo noted. “Then Peter suggested the Dylan Thomas. […] I can’t imagine a more exciting way to have Peter be in your show than doing this Dylan Thomas poem that’s a gentle poem, but he does it with this rage — how it’s supposed to be read. It’s amazing.”.

Recent findings suggest that volunteering to speak when Ray (Michael Hitchcock) gets overwhelmed, Wendell spends a few seconds scrolling to find the right poem (“Do not go gentle into that good night”) and then tears into it with vigor. Dinklage’s recitation is more of a resuscitation — powerful enough to wake the dead, it wakes Lee up, snapping him into the present and bringing him back to life.

“When he’s doing the poem, he came in at a 10,” Harjo mentioned. “The only direction I gave him was, ‘What if you build to that?’ And that’s what he did, and it was just unbelievably great.”.

In a recent development, “That one is violent and abrupt,” Hawke mentioned. “It’s a friend shaking you up.”.

In a recent development, in Hawke’s case, Lee’s friend was his real friend. He knew Dinklage “loved poetry,” and he even knew a little bit about what his fellow actor would bring to this poem.

Sources indicate that “This is where collaboration is really mysterious about how it works and when it works really well,” Hawke said. “I’ve been friends with Peter Dinklage since, I don’t know, 1990. […] We both arrived in Upcoming York around the same time, and we used to sit around and tie one on and try to flirt with girls and read poems. We used to geek out about how much we loved the ways people would read poems in the old days. If you hear Dylan Thomas read a poem or you hear Orson Wells read a poem, they weren’t afraid of feeling or emotion or a theatricality. They weren’t afraid of passion — actual passion — and caring and looking foolish.”.

“We’re living in an age of irony and cynicism and detachment, and this definition of cool being that you don’t care. Whereas the definition when I was growing up was Bob Marley and John Lennon and Miles Davis and those guys cared a tremendous amount. They weren’t detached. They were completely attached. So for me to watch Peter bring that to his performance was like, ‘Let me show you kids how to do a poem!’ [laughs] ‘You got to do it like your life depends on it.'”.

According to recent reports, “The key to that scene is the interaction between him and Lee,” Harjo stated. “I love that he’s watching Lee the whole time. It’s like there’s no one else in the room and he’s doing it for Lee. I love that.”.

“The camera does pick up subconscious,” Hawke remarked. “A lot of times I’ll see work that might be good, but it has no subconscious to it. I can tell there’s no secret sewn into the filmmaking. And Sterlin loves — you can call it poetry, you can call it whatever you want — but [he loves] when there’s multiple layers happening. […] And so for me, I’m not just sitting there with an actor doing this scene. I’ve known this guy for 30 years and I know what this poem means to him, and he knows me.”.

“If there was an Academy Award for Best Single Scene, I would give it to Peter Dinklage in our show.”.

Recent findings suggest that while Dinklage may have to settle for an Emmy, Harjo had to write the other big finale monologue for an actual Oscar winner. At the reception, Lee’s daughter Francis (Ryan Kiera Armstrong) reads a passage from her grandfather’s journal, written shortly after Lee Jr. was born, as a way to honor her ancestor. Then, as Francis speaks Senior’s words, Senior appears seated behind her, and Tommy Lee Jones takes over the scene.

“The bigger thing about that monologue is I knew it was coming,” Harjo said. “I was like, ‘Oh shit, I got to write this thing for Tommy Lee Jones.’ I kind of had Tommy Lee Jones dialed in through the whole season. I felt like I could really write his voice. But when it came to that monologue, I’m like, ‘God, he’s already known for one of the best monologues in the world at the end of ‘No Country for Old Men,’ and I can either try to do a fancy monologue that isn’t like that at all, or I could lean into the fact that Cormac McCarthy and the Coen brothers did this really well already, and there’s no way that I don’t know that as a filmmaker. So I’m going to lean into it and almost give homage to that speech.'”.

“And that’s what I did. It has this bit of nostalgia. It also has this magic to it and this dreamlike quality to what he’s doing,” Harjo stated. “The character is such an internal person that the only way you’re going to get those monologues is through a journal when he thinks it’s the privacy of himself and his journal. He’s expressing things that he wouldn’t normally express out loud.”.

Industry observers note that “Not to toot my own horn, but I feel like I nailed it,” he said, laughing. “Of course, it filters through Tommy Lee Jones and all of a sudden it’s like this fucking amazing thing that he does. It was wonderful being on set. Just watching him give that, it was unbelievable. I could have used any take and it would’ve been amazing in a different way.”.

Throughout the monologue, Lee sits in thoughtful silence. He’s not only absorbing what his father wrote and remembering who he was; he’s also recognizing his shifting role as a son who’s now a father. There’s a connection across generations. Yes, his responsibility to his daughter means avoiding repeating his dad’s mistakes, which Lee is well-aware of, but it also means honoring his father’s better intentions, like the ones he voiced in that journal and Francis is voicing again now.

“Lee’s adamant that he’s nothing like his father,” Hawke said. “The first thought I had is, ‘All right, this is why Lee Raybon is obsessed with the truth: It’s that his father was a chronic liar.’ If you grew up in a house where your parent was really comfortable lying to you, you would get obsessed with people in power misleading you, and that would really drive you.”.

“But then as we played the scenes deeper, I realized that Lee was lying to himself; that he was just as manipulative as his father is. He just does it in the name of truth. All this bad behavior that he was in denial of, he’d actually internalized it, and he was so much like his dad that he was completely blind to it, which is behavior I’ve seen in so many friends. It’s amazing. But I had to live through it. I didn’t get it when I was reading it. I got it when I was playing it, and that was very powerful for me.”.

One way Harjo & co. illustrate Lee’s development over the course of Season 2 is simple: He listens. Instead of shouting, pontificating, or generally causing chaos, Lee spends much of the finale hearing what everyone around him has to say. Even when he’s up his own ass or annoying the hell out of folks, he has a community who cares about him, and their steady presence in his life is what eventually breaks down his defenses.

“The first [wave] is Peter reading that poem, and then the second one is gentle and persuasive where my daughter is revealing to me that my father did love me,” Hawke remarked. “Part of the thing you learn watching this show is that Lee feels like he has to conquer the world to be worthy of self-respect. His daughter is saying, ‘It’s right here for you, and it always has been.'”.

Sources indicate that while another monologue played a significant role in how the episode plays out — Ginger’s speech to Francis, outside the bookstore — that moment wasn’t about Lee. (“The whole idea was Ginger and Francis don’t really get to hang out, but they are alike,” Harjo said. “Ginger immediately recognizes it and probably also knows that she had a father that was a lot like Lee.”) So his final wave comes from a curious source.

In a recent development, “The third one is just this final little moment that happens with Vickey (Abbie Cobb) when she tells him his fortune is bad and he sees it as a good thing. He understands that everything is point of view, and for him, towers coming down would be good.”.

“Those are the three steps that I think are designed to get Lee back on his feet again,” Hawke stated. “That push him to be like, ‘All right, you know what? I’m not quitting. I’m going to keep being me, and I’m going to be a better version of me.'”.

How he’s feeling when Season 3 starts is anyone’s guess, and that assumes a renewal that’s yet to be declared is still in the offing from FX. But one thing’s for sure: If Lee comes back, he’ll be a changed man — and he won’t be alone.

“The Lowdown” is available on FX and Hulu.

Stephen King's horror adaptation gets a upcoming life.

It has been revealed that king's career began with his first novel, Carrie, published in 1974, which allowed him to become a full-time writer and later be named the King of Horror. King has a career spanning six decades and has published over 50 books and around 200 short stories, selling over 350 million copies of his work worldwide. Over the years, his novels have received many adaptations in movies, TV series, radio demonstrates, stage plays, and more. Now, a forgotten adaptation is returning in a brand-new way.

In a recent development, the adaptation of King's novel from 1991, titled Needful Things, is getting a stunning new release. The 1993 movie Needful Things is set to get a 4K UHD and Blu-ray limited edition SteelBook release, with pre-orders open from December 1 ahead of its release on January 20, 2027. ViaVision Entertainment is releasing Needful Things in a whole new way with only 1,500 copies available. The movie has been restored from the original 35mm camera negative with both the 121-minute theatrical cut and the 191-minute television cut.

Stephen King’s best-selling horror novel comes to life in Needful Things, the ultimate tale of buyer beware, starring Ed Harris, Max von Sydow, Bonnie Bedelia, and J.T. Walsh.

A new shop has opened in the quiet Maine town of Castle Rock, and its mysterious proprietor, Leland Gaunt, seems to stock exactly what each customer has always wanted. But Gaunt’s prices are steeper than they appear. Before long, he begins to set the whole town against itself - and only Sheriff Alan Pangborn suspects that the stranger’s wares are more dangerous than they look.

Sources indicate that the Needful Things release includes three discs: Disc One is the 4K UHD theatrical cut of the movie, Disc Two is the Blu-ray theatrical cut, and Disc Three is also a Blu-ray, but the 191-minute television cut includes interviews with film historian Dr. Simon Brown and screenwriter W.D. Ritcher.

Needful Things, released in 1994, starred Ed Harris, Max Von Sydow, Bonnie Bedelia, Amanda Plummer, Ray McKinnon, and J.T. Walsh. The movie adaptation was directed by Fraser Clarke Heston and achieved a 35% rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes, with a 44% rating from audiences. Reviews from critics stated, "There's just not enough menace in this movie adaptation of the Stephen King novel," and "A devilishly fun and mysterious mix of the supernatural and personal stories of drama, crime, and all sorts of small town issues.".

King's novel was a commercial bestseller and sold over 1.5 million copies. Unfortunately, the adaptation only grossed around $15 million and failed to become a huge success.

Needful Things' stunning new release arrives on January 20, 2027.

Among iOS 27’s many fresh features is a great change for anyone with multiple iPhones: you can now keep the same phone number on two iPhones via iPhone Handoff.

With iOS 27, Apple introduces big AI upgrades like Siri AI, plus exciting fresh features for apps like Wallet, Messages, Notes, and also CarPlay and AirPods.

But the revision also has a lot of smaller, more niche improvements.

One such addition is iPhone Handoff, which enables switching seamlessly between two iPhones using the same phone number.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:.

After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.

To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The message “Switched to this iPhone” will display at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff.

Most owners will never need this feature. But if you’re someone who, for whatever reason, has separate devices that you want on the same number, iOS 27 has the solution.

According to recent reports, I feel like I’m exactly who this feature was made for. After years of running dual SIM, I now have a personal line on my Duo and work line on an 18 Pro. Going out with friends, family, etc, I’d love to bring one phone again while bringing both numbers with me, but keeping work system access to a specific, separate device. Only current problem is waiting for Verizon to activate the feature and then see if it actually works well.

If you’re trying to decide between an iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, perhaps iPhone Handoff is Apple’s subtle way of saying: “Why choose?”.

So far carrier support is limited (here’s the latest list), but Apple prepares to expand iPhone Handoff to more carriers soon.

The film and his performance are eligible for this year’s Oscars, and “I Swear” is now streaming on Netflix.].

When Robert Aramayo signed on to play Scottish Tourette’s activist John Davidson in filmmaker Kirk Jones’ biopic “I Swear,” he could scarcely imagine where the film would take him.

In a recent development, A hit in the UK, the film netted Aramayo a pair of BAFTA wins earlier in the year, as the British actor won both the vaunted Rising Star Award (previous winners include James McAvoy, John Boyega, Tom Holland, Tom Hardy, and those are just some of its biggest names) and the Best Actor trophy (beating out Timothée Chalamet, Leonardo DiCaprio, Ethan Hawke, Jesse Plemons, and eventual Oscar winner Michael B. Jordan). Related Stories ‘The Lowdown’ Season 2 Finale Hinges on Two Monologues — Let Ethan Hawke and Sterlin Harjo Break Them Down Danielle Brooks Shares Insights from the Indie Success of ‘If I Go Will They Miss Me’.

But that’s hardly all that happened at the February awards show, which was instantly and forever marred by a number of loud, racist outbursts from Davidson himself that were directed at “Sinners” stars Jordan, Delroy Lindo, Wunmi Mosaku, and more. The fallout from the incident was both swift and prolonged, and will likely impact the domestic release of “I Swear,” which is rolling out in stateside theaters now.

Aramayo’s performance in the film is indeed star-making and awards-worthy, as he brings sensitivity and great courage to his portrayal of Davidson, following him from his earliest symptoms through his current passionate activism. Hopefully, viewers can see and appreciate the work on its own merits, and get to know Aramayo much better, though he has previously appeared in plenty of projects recognizable to American audiences, from “The Empty Man” to “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” to a little thing called “Game of Thrones” (young Ned Stark!).

Ahead, Aramayo tells IndieWire about his deep research for the role, everything BAFTAs, and what he hopes will come from more people seeing the film and, hopefully, understanding Tourette’s all the better.

The following interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

It has been revealed that indieWire: When I saw the film at TIFF in September, I did my due diligence before I reviewed it, and learned that John is a huge figure in the UK, but relatively unknown in America. How much did you know about him before this film?

Robert Aramayo: John’s made a lot of documentaries, but the big one that probably had the most impact was “John’s Not Mad,” and that was in 1989. So if you speak to people who were around then, they have a lot of very personal stories about watching that documentary and being like, “Wow, is this Tourette’s? What’s Tourette’s?”.

So when you get the script, are you someone who then wants to do more research into him, or do you feel like the script is the thing?

Recent findings suggest that the production team and Kirk were so gracious, and they gave me so much time. I think they were like, “Oh, yeah, take a couple of months or something to research and stuff.” I was really thankful for that. The first thing that I did was to meet John; I met him very promptly. And then I went away for a month, and I spent that time gaining as much knowledge as I could about Tourette’s and what it is. That was through watching the documentaries, watching YouTube videos, and reading books.

Sources indicate that I based myself in Galashiels and spent weeks with John, just following him around and spending as much time with him as I could. And also traveling through Scotland, meeting people, mainly through [support organization] Tourette Scotland, who lived with Tourette’s as well. I wanted to have, I don’t know, a more expansive view of Tourette’s than just John. Obviously, John was my main focus, though.

When you’re getting ready to meet John, what were you expecting and anticipating? What were you nervous about?

Sources indicate that I don’t know what I felt, really. I was so filled with anxiety about, oh my word, am I going to do this? I wanted John to like me. I was already feeling, God, this is going to be a really significant challenge. And I met him within days of saying yes.

But then, when I met him, one thing that struck me straight away was his knowledge. He’s got a really amazing knowledge about, obviously, Tourette’s, but also a lot of neurodiversity and how it lives, other conditions that exist with Tourette’s, and stuff like that. He’s got a lot of thoughts about how we can do better and help young people and things like that. He’s very forthcoming with it.

He’s got so much heart. He’s such an amazing, welcoming, supportive man that I was just like, wow, this is a really impressive person that I’m meeting here. Of course, then your anxiety and the responsibility meter have gone through the roof.

Just watching the film, I learned so much about what Tourette’s can entail and the very wide spectrum of symptoms that people can have. What was the most unexpected thing you learned about it during your research?

Recent findings suggest that A couple of things really that had a really big impact on me straight away, and that sort of broke my perception of what I thought Tourette’s was, that anything can be a tic, and that it’s so singular to the person. So if you’ve met one person with Tourette’s, someone stated to me, you’ve met one person with Tourette’s. That was a big thing.

Recent findings suggest that and also the fact that there’s a lot of tics that you just don’t see. There’s tics that you don’t see as tics because anything can be a tic, or there’s tics that exist only in somebody’s mind, and things like that, tics linked with OCD. Just the complexity of it was massive.

I learned some statistics recently, which I found really interesting: One in 50 kids in America live with persistent tic disorder, and one in 160 live with Tourette’s, so it’s unbelievably common, it’s everywhere. We have met people with Tourette’s, we meet them all the time. It was part of the experience of the film as well, we met loads of people who were living with Tourette’s undiagnosed. 50 percent of people who live with Tourette’s in the U.S. are undiagnosed, and that was true for us in the UK as well in our experience. Maybe the thing is that we don’t know that that’s what’s happening. That made me think, wow, there’s a real educational piece to this as well.

Recent findings suggest that you are playing someone who is a real person who has been captured on film for many years. People know what he looks like, they know what he sounds like. How do you find the line between impersonation and impression in your performance?

According to recent reports, I never wanted to impersonate John. I think I would’ve gone the wrong way if that was what I was thinking. You have to, at a certain point, take ownership of the character and try and make him your own. I was lucky because there was so much that I needed to learn, so for so long, I wasn’t thinking about performance or playing him at all. I was just trying to immerse myself as much as I could in everything, anything that I could get my hands on. Then, at certain point, I moved to thinking about how I was going to try and play my version of John.

In a [narrative] film, you get the opportunity to maybe show a little bit more [than a documentary]. A documentary film crew comes into somebody’s life and they can capture what they can capture, but we could capture way more intimate moments throughout the whole film that John had spoken to.

We could show the moments where he is on his own, whether there’s been an impact or how he’s feeling or his emotional life, how things change over time and stuff like that, and hopefully try and do it with truth and authenticity.

You attended Juilliard, which always seems a little, “Oooohhh, he’s Juilliard-trained.”.

But now that you’re a few years out of school, what are the pieces of training that are proving to be most useful to you?

I think that acting teachers and drama school is vocabulary, really. At the time, certain things that teachers would say to me had a massive impact on me and really opened me up to other ways of looking at things, and other things are only impacting me now, as I keep working and as I get older. I think that’s the beauty of drama school, you get flooded with all of this stuff, and then you’re going, “Oh, that’s what they were talking about.” And then there’s things that my teachers would consistently say, “You’ve got to work on this, you’ve got to work on this,” and I’m still working on it. It’s like a toolbox, and every now and again you go, “Oh, yeah, that’s what I need.”.

They also made us do liberal arts which — I’m from Yorkshire, I don’t even know what liberal arts meant — but I’d encounter Nietzsche and Plato and all this stuff. I had no time at all to digest anything, but I’d read it and be like, “I don’t really know what’s going on here, but I think this is going to be notable one day. I think I’m going to reread this one day!”.

What was the morning of the BAFTA nominations like for you?

I knew it was happening that morning. I remember talking to my agent, and we just didn’t speak about it, but we both knew that they were coming out that morning or whatever, so we had a really chill conversation about something else. [Laughs] I put it on in the background, because I thought we had a chance at, I don’t know, something, and then I heard that Peter had been nominated and I was so happy for him. I was elated for him.

So, I was just in that, and I was doing the dishes, and I was like, “Wow, that’s so cool. I can’t wait to go text him.” And then they said my name, and I just absolutely couldn’t believe it. My agent called me back straight away and was like, “Oh, my God.” It was an amazing feeling, but it was really unexpected because I was still really, really sort of overwhelmed by the Rising Star thing.

You genuinely looked so surprised when you won Best Actor at the show. I feel like I would black out in that moment. Do you remember what that moment felt like?

In a recent development, yeah, because I almost did! I had this weird physical reaction where I sort of went back [pantomimes sitting way back], and I think somebody grabbed me. I think I would’ve just kept going. I would’ve fallen off my chair or something.

Sources indicate that I honestly couldn’t believe it. I’m honestly not sure I still can believe that that’s something that happened to me, because for someone like me to be in that group of people blew my mind. I felt like, “Wow, and there I am, that’s my name.” To me, that was the thing that sort of really, really, really, really blew me away. When it happened, yes, it all just becomes a blur, and I’m running down the stairs, and I don’t know what the hell I’m going to say.

Obviously, other things happened at the awards show involving John. As someone who had seen the film, I felt like I had a greater grasp on what was happening; I had that context. Now that the film is coming out in America, what hopes do you have for people seeing the film and how that might impact that conversation?

Sources indicate that I think lots of people watch the film, and they feel like their education around Tourette’s has improved and increased, and that would be amazing [if that continued]. I think it’s important to acknowledge that … Tourette’s has an impact on a person who’s ticcing, and the same tic obviously has an impact on the person who’s receiving the tic or impacted by the tic. And it’s important to acknowledge that, because that is what it is. Coprolalia, which is the tic that John has, that tic, it’s not saying what you think, it’s saying the worst thing imaginable. That’s how it was described to me.

Sources indicate that I hope people watch the film. And I hope people watch the film and think, “Oh, I’ve learned something about Tourette’s.” I hope that people watch the film from the community, because that’s been an amazing thing as well. People watching it who have lived with Tourette’s or lived with another neurodiverse condition have reached out and said, “I see myself in this.” You want people to go to the movies and enjoy the film, but if people go home and Google “John Davidson” or Google “Tourette’s,” that’d be amazing.

The film is going to introduce you to a much larger audience, but you’ve also been in some massive hits before this one. Which is a fun way to ask: Do you know that “The Empty Man” has a huge cult fandom?

Sources indicate that [Laughs] I’ve been told this. What an experience. I loved making that film. It was a long journey with it, and I learned a lot. And it was my first movie that I’d done with James Badge Dale, and I did another one with him as well. And I really, really liked working with him. He’s a really nice guy, and he’s a really talented actor. And the director, David [Prior], was wonderful. I learned a lot on that film. I love that people love that film.

You are also in the “Lord of the Rings” world as well. Are you going to be turning out to see “The Hunt for Gollum”?

It has been revealed that I’m so excited. I can’t wait. I’m a massive fan of the Peter Jackson films. I can’t wait to see what they do with it. It’s a really interesting story. I’m glad that they’re doing it and doing it properly.

Now that you’ve had what feels like a big breakthrough, what sort of things are you pursuing next?

In a recent development, what do I want to do next? I don’t know! I feel lucky to just be an actor, to work. I’ve been lucky enough to work with some incredible people on “I Swear,” to work with Kirk and Peter and Shirley and Maxine. People like that, you learn, you grow, you get better. And so if I can just keep doing it, I’ll be happy.

That Rising Star Award feels like a lot of pressure!

According to recent reports, I just feel really, really grateful for everyone who voted for me. It’s such a cool award that the public, the British public, vote for you. I feel so grateful for everyone who voted for me. I just feel very, very grateful for the whole thing, for everything, and mainly that people hopefully watch the film and talk about it.

Hannah covers horror, sci-fi, and games at Collider, where she writes news and features, reviews new releases, and interviews the people who make them. She’s helping build out Collider’s gaming coverage, with Pokémon as one of her specialties. If she isn’t writing about a monster, she’s probably watching one on a tape from her VHS collection.

According to recent reports, in the decades that Marvel has spent exploring alternate realities, few have presented such wildly different possibilities for mutantkind as House of M and Days of Future Past. The former saw Wanda Maximoff reshape reality, elevating mutants to positions of power and placing Magneto at the head of a royal family. The latter presented a horrifying future in which Sentinels had systematically decimated the mutant population. Naturally, Marvel has found a way to make life considerably worse for the inhabitants of both worlds.

Recent findings suggest that with Avengers: Doomsday and Avengers: Secret Wars on the horizon, Marvel Comics has been revisiting some of the major events that inspired the MCU’s upcoming crossover. Among them are the incursions that preceded Jonathan Hickman’s 2015 Secret Wars event, in which collisions between parallel universes threatened the existence of the entire multiverse. Marvel is now exploring what happened to some of its most recognizable alternate realities during those catastrophic events.

Marvel’s X-Men: Incursions #1, written by Alex Paknadel and illustrated by Jim Towe, is officially available following its November 18 release. The 32-page one-shot brings the worlds of House of M and Days of Future Past into direct conflict, giving Kate Pryde just eight hours to prevent both realities from being destroyed. The older version of Kitty Pryde finds herself exploring a world where mutants enjoy the freedoms she spent much of her life fighting for.

Four people, four completely different ideas of what it means to have somebody in your corner. Here is who picked up, what they would ask of you, and what you would get back.

According to recent reports, you want the friend who does not leave. Steve is the one who turns up at the door without being asked, who remembers what you said you were worried about, and who has never once made you audition for his attention.

You want the friend who is genuinely exhausting and completely worth it. Tony will forget your birthday, then build you something at four in the morning that you did not know you needed, and hand it over as though it were nothing.

Sources indicate that you want the friend who replies in four seconds and apologises for it. Peter is earnest in a way that is almost unfashionable, and he will take on far more than he can carry rather than admit that he is struggling.

Recent findings suggest that you want the friend who insults your shoes, fixes your phone and then quietly rearranges your entire life for the better. Shuri does not do soft reassurance, and that is the reason you would believe her when she says you are fine.

In a recent development, X-Men: Incursions is the first of five one-shots revisiting the events leading up to Secret Wars. The next installment, Spider-Man: Incursions #1, pits Gwen Stacy against Mayday Parker, the daughter of Peter Parker and Mary Jane Watson from the MC2 universe. Fantastic Four: Incursions will also explore an alternate version of Marvel’s First Family with gamma-based powers. Perhaps the most exciting upcoming release for longtime X-Men fans is January’s X-Men ’92: Incursions, which brings together two generations of animated mutant heroes. The X-Men of the beloved 1990s animated series and its modern revival, X-Men '97, will collide with their younger counterparts from X-Men: Evolution, with writers Craig Kyle and Christopher Yost behind the crossover.

X-Men: Incursions #1 is available now for $4.99.

Industry observers note that if you picked up a latest iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo this fall, or you’re shopping for someone with an iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch, there’s a good chance you’ve been holding out on purchasing accessories until all of the Black Friday deals started. We’ve got you covered with some great deals on premium accessories for nearly every Apple device on your list.

It has been revealed that ESR has been making Apple accessories since 2009, and that track record has made it a trustworthy name for the more than 123 million people who use its products to protect their Apple devices and make them more versatile. Here’s a look at what’s included in ESR’s Black Friday lineup and who each one is for.

According to recent reports, if someone on your shopping list picked up an iPhone Duo, a case is the first thing they need, and it’s also the hardest one to get right. As we’ve seen with Android foldables, you’re protecting two halves, a hinge, and a phone that changes shape throughout the day as you use it, all without adding bulk to a device people bought because it folds thin. ESR has two options for iPhone Duo owners, and the choice mostly comes down to the look you want to achieve.

The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand is your choice if you want to show off your iPhone Duo’s colors. It combines a rigid polycarbonate and acrylic back with a softer TPU frame. The rigid back keeps the case from flexing and lets the iPhone Duo’s design show through, while the flexible frame absorbs the shock if you drop it (please don’t).

The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand is perfect for those who want a more premium look for their iPhone Duo. It’s made from organic silicone leather with a soft, skin-friendly feel and a stain-resistant finish. If you’ve ever used a light-colored leather case before, you know it usually demonstrates every stain and smudge it comes across, but ESR built the Atelier to resist daily wear and wipe clean.

Both cases share ESR’s Flex Stand, and it’s one of the most innovative and versatile parts of the lineup. It’s a 180-degree rotating stand made from zinc alloy, so it holds its shape even after months of propping up your iPhone. A precision hinge with damping control lets it open smoothly and lock at the angle you choose, whether the iPhone Duo is folded or unfolded, and ESR says it has passed 3,000 open-and-close tests. In real life, that means propping the iPhone Duo open on a desk for a video call or on an airplane tray table for a movie, then using the stand as a grip when you’re holding it.

It has been revealed that both cases add extra hinge protection and raised edges where a foldable is most exposed. If you follow our MagSafe Monday column, you know magnetic strength really matters for MagSafe wallets, car mounts, etc. The Classic Hybrid has 1,500g of magnetic hold, and the Atelier has 1,400g.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case for iPhone Duo is 15% off.

The same two incredible cases come in iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max versions, and they also fit the iPhone 17 Pro and Pro Max. The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case with Camera Control and Flex Stand has a clear back, a TPU frame, and a PU anti-yellowing coating. In simple terms, TPU is the flexible, shock-absorbing plastic used in most case frames, and it’s also what usually turns clear cases slightly yellow the longer you use them, so ESR adds a polyurethane (PU) coating to shield it. ESR upgraded the case’s UV protection for longer-lasting resistance to yellowing, and it’s SGS-certified for anti-yellowing. A clear case is supposed to show off your iPhone’s color, so staying clear longer is the whole point. The ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case with Flex Stand retains the same soft silicone leather and stain-resistant finish as the iPhone Duo version.

On these models, the Flex Stand adjusts from 15 to 69 degrees for portrait and landscape viewing. That has you covered for StandBy mode on your nightstand and a show over your lunch break, with no separate stand to carry around.

Recent findings suggest that protection is where the two cases differ. ESR rates the Classic Hybrid for 4x military-grade protection with 16-foot drop protection, plus a full-coverage camera bar. The Atelier is rated for 3x military-grade protection, including 12-foot drop protection, and features a soft microfiber lining. Military-grade refers to the MIL-STD-810 drop test, which uses a 4-foot drop, so 4x and 3x mean ESR rates the cases for four and three times that height. Both include a built-in Camera Control cover and raised edges, and both use a precise magnetic ring layout that automatically aligns with MagSafe chargers, car mounts, wallets, and batteries.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Classic Hybrid Magnetic Case is up to 28% off, and the ESR Atelier Vegan Leather Magnetic Case is up to 37% off.

A case protects everything except the part you touch all day. The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector covers the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, and the name is worth unpacking. Armorite is ESR’s line of toughened screen protectors, and the Pro version is made with Accessory Glass by Corning™. Corning has made the durable glass in Apple products since the very first iPhone, so in non-tech speak, this is glass from a trustworthy name rather than generic tempered glass.

Why it matters: ESR claims the protector delivers 10x the impact absorption of generic protectors, and Corning’s lab testing shows up to 2x better scratch performance and up to 25% less scratch visibility for its Accessory Glass. When you drop your iPhone or toss it in a pocket with your keys, the protector takes the hit instead of your screen. An anti-reflective coating reduces light reflection to just 2.3% while maintaining 94% optical transmittance, resulting in less glare outside and truer color. Edge-to-edge coverage leaves no gaps for dust to collect.

Industry observers note that installation is the part most people dread on a brand-new iPhone, and ESR’s UltraFit tray handles it in two steps. Pull the tab, and the tray’s design clears dust and pushes out air bubbles as the glass goes down. Long gone are the days when you needed “professional installation” for a screen protector to look great.

Black Friday deal: The ESR UltraFit Armorite Pro Screen Protector is 15% off.

Industry observers note that holiday travel usually means one open outlet, an iPhone, a laptop, an e-reader, etc., that all need power, and cables left at home. The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger builds the cable in. It has a braided cable that extends to 3.1 feet and fully retracts into the charger, and ESR rates it for 20,000 pulls and 10,000 bends. In a recent development, it’s rated at 45 watts and delivers up to 60 watts of dynamic power, enough to fast-charge phones and laptops, and it works with iPhone Duo, iPhone 15 through 18, and Android phones like Galaxy and Pixel. It supports PD 3.2 AVS, which in plain English means the charger and your device talk to each other, and the charger fine-tunes the power it sends to exactly what that device asks for. ESR states it can charge an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max to 50% in about 15 minutes. It’s also TÜV-certified, meaning an independent testing organization has verified its safety features.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Xtend 45W Retractable Charger is up to 32% off from November 20 through December 1.

For the student or anyone who does real work on an iPad, the ESR Shift Keyboard Case makes for an incredible gift. The Bluetooth keyboard attaches magnetically and comes off when you don’t need it, so you can type an essay at a desk, then pull the keyboard away to watch something on the couch or sketch with the iPad flat on a table.

Industry observers note that ESR built the Shift around five modes designed to make your iPad even more versatile. Productivity mode lets you detach the keyboard and type over Bluetooth, so the iPad can sit on a desk while the keyboard sits on your lap. Landscape mode adjusts from 20 to 75 degrees for typing and watching, Portrait mode holds 70 degrees for reading, browsing in Safari, or making a FaceTime call, and Drawing mode drops to a stable 20 degrees for sketching and editing with your Apple Pencil. Hands-On mode lets you hold the iPad like a regular tablet. An iPad is a laptop one minute and a tablet the next, and the Shift is designed to keep up with all of your iPad use cases.

For a student, that means taking notes in class with the keyboard attached, then detaching it to annotate a PDF or review flashcards on the couch. For someone who travels for work, it means answering email on a tray table, then pulling the keyboard off to watch a movie on the flight home. One case covers both, and the keyboard pairs and reconnects easily when you snap it back on.

Sources indicate that the trackpad is fully clickable and supports all the multi-touch gestures you already use on your iPad. Apple Pencil gets a home too. ESR’s Dual Smart Pencil Storage uses a magnetic holder and an elastic sleeve, so your Pencil stays with your iPad instead of rolling around the bottom of your bag. Its Air Guard corners protect your iPad when it’s stowed away.

The ESR Shift Keyboard Case comes in versions for iPad Pro 11-inch and 13-inch (M4 and M5), iPad Air 11-inch and 13-inch (including the new M4 models), and iPad (A16), so whichever iPad you’re trying to take to the next level of productivity, there’s a Shift that fits it.

Black Friday deal: The ESR Shift Keyboard Case is up to 25% off, depending on your iPad model.

Sources indicate that have you ever dropped your AirPods case and watched the earbuds go flying? With the Cyber FlickLock, you won’t have to worry about that. We’ve covered FlickLock in MagSafe Monday before, but let’s recap it.

When the internal latch is engaged, the magnets line up to attract each other and hold the lid shut with maximum force, adding a second layer of security. Slide the button, and the magnets shift to repel each other, so the lid pops open with one hand. ESR claims the slide mechanism has been tested over 20,000 times.

Recent findings suggest that the result is that your AirPods stay in the case if you drop it. Black Friday deal: The ESR Cyber FlickLock and Pulse FlickLock Magnetic Cases are both 20% off.

Recent findings suggest that the ESR Equinox Watch Band is a quick pick for anyone who works out in the morning while tracking progress with Apple Watch, then heads to the office. A pin-and-fold lock keeps it secure, and it’s made from HNBR, a durable, skin-friendly synthetic rubber that resists water and tearing, with ventilation cutouts for all-day comfort. Prime Video Successfully Replaces The Boys After 5 Seasons

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Screenrant

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that turning a controversial, divisive, and extremely graphic comic series into a live-action R-rated show was a huge gamble for Prime Video, yet The Boys rapidly became one of the platform's biggest hits.
  • Recent findings suggest that unsurprisingly, Prime Video isn't letting go of the franchise after The Boys' series finale aired earlier this year, but despite Vought Rising and The Boys: Mexico being in development, the main show's conclusion leaves the door open for a newly introduced flagship superhero show to take over the platform.
  • It has been revealed that while The Boys is undoubtedly the more mainstream series, Invincible found success alongside it and is often considered the better of Prime Video's two main R-rated superhero projects.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that turning a controversial, divisive, and extremely graphic comic series into a live-action R-rated show was a huge gamble for Prime Video, yet The Boys rapidly became one of the platform's biggest hits. Not only did it vastly exceed expectations to become one of the greatest superhero masterpieces of the decade, but it also gained a huge following, making it one of the most talked-about highlights throughout its seven-year journey.

Recent findings suggest that unsurprisingly, Prime Video isn't letting go of the franchise after The Boys' series finale aired earlier this year, but despite Vought Rising and The Boys: Mexico being in development, the main show's conclusion leaves the door open for a newly introduced flagship superhero show to take over the platform. Luckily, Invincible's growing success makes it the perfect replacement.

It has been revealed that while The Boys is undoubtedly the more mainstream series, Invincible found success alongside it and is often considered the better of Prime Video's two main R-rated superhero projects. Like The Boys, it is also a comic adaptation; however, Invincible is much more faithful to the source material, and as a result, tends to be more consistent.

Still, despite building its own dedicated fanbase and earning many plaudits, Invincible has never truly escaped The Boys' shadow, until now. With Invincible season 4 ending on a high, the stage is set perfectly for season 5, taking the project to the same number of seasons as The Boys, and with no signs of it slowing down, there couldn't be a more fitting replacement.

With season 5 scheduled to premiere in February 2027, Invincible is approaching the same milestone as The Boys, but there is still so much more story to tell. Having deviated heavily from the comics and opted for a largely different story, The Boys decided to call it quits after five seasons and 40 episodes, which proved to be the right decision.

Had it dragged on any longer, the show's reputation may have tanked even further, and there's still a variety of spinoffs that give fans of the franchise a reason to stick around. In contrast, Invincible is essentially a one-to-one adaptation, and while there was an Atom Eve special episode between seasons 1 and 2, the project has largely focused on bringing Robert Kirkman's original story to TV while adding a few extras.

Sources indicate that so far, the series has covered about half of the comics' story, meaning we could still get another four seasons before it's all stated and done. There's also the opportunity to expand this universe on-screen with more specials or miniseries, potentially following the likes of Tech Jacket or Battle Beast, who also have their own comic run.

Even without these though, Invincible will comfortably outlast The Boys and should come close to doubling its season and episode count, especially since season 6 is already confirmed. Considering the project is still extremely popular and continues to get more intense, it's hard to imagine it getting canceled, meaning it is likely to see out its entire vision.

Invincible is already set to break the record as Prime Video's longest-running animated show, and if it does reach season 8 or beyond, it could become the platform's longest show ever. This would make it a historic hit that transcends The Boys, and assuming it avoids a controversial ending like its competitor, Invincible is poised to have a superior legacy as well.

Industry observers note that while Vought Rising will bring The Boys franchise back into the limelight in 2027, Invincible will inevitably step up as Prime Video's main superhero series. Having already accumulated a lively fan base as well as an immaculate reputation, Invincible has all the tools needed to step up, and the extra marketing could do wonders for this already successful hit.

In a recent development, seasons 3 and 4 produced eight episodes that earned a 9 and above rating on IMDb, which means one in every two episodes achieved this incredible score. Two of them even earned a rare 9.9, showing the quality is certainly there. The fact that the story was left in such a good place means there's no reason to expect Invincible to decline, making it a seamless replacement for The Boys.

It's not without its flaws, as production delays have hurt the show in the past, while there remain concerns about the animation. However, recent years have seen improvement in both areas, particularly the length between seasons, and the fact that Invincible is releasing annually makes it even easier to promote and build an audience.

With a live-action movie supposedly still in production and a recent video game release, the franchise continues to evolve, which only helps make the show feel bigger. Invincible's ability to switch genres, feature plenty of humor during its brutal story, and throw shade at itself all adds to what makes it so special, proving why Prime Video should continue investing heavily.

Even if it never quite matches the mainstream appeal of The Boys, Invincible remains a massive gem that the platform can utilize for years to come, and if they were to give it a bigger budget and iron out any lingering issues, the superhero series could become one of Prime Video's greatest hits of all time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, samsung’s flagship soundbars have reached the point where the yearly upgrades are more about refinement than reinvention, and that is pretty much the story with the Samsung HW-Q990H—and this 2026 model is on sale for $500 off for Black Friday, down to $1,497.99 from $1,997.99. That's its lowest price to date.

Recent findings suggest that samsung kept the same 11.1.4-channel setup from the older HW-Q990F, including the soundbar, wireless subwoofer, and two rear speakers, but leaned harder into software this time around—features like the SpaceFit Sound Pro automatically adjust the sound depending on your room layout, and unlike some auto-calibration features that barely change anything, this one reportedly shifts the audio balance in noticeable ways. Sometimes it improves dialogue clarity and bass response. Other times, you may prefer tweaking things yourself with the built-in seven-band EQ.

The system also handles basically every major audio format, supports wireless Dolby Atmos with compatible Samsung TVs, and includes 4K 120Hz HDMI passthrough for people gaming on a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X. That noted, while the bass is strong for a compact subwoofer, it compresses when you push the volume near maximum, so it's not perfect for huge spaces or people who want nightclub-level output. SSH is a GUI framework

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (818 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zydra

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "One thing about which fish know exactly nothing is water." — Marshall McLuhan.
  • SSH is a tool so ubiquitous that we've forgotten what it actually is: a multiplexed, encrypted byte stream accessible on a cross-platform rendering engine that ships on every laptop, server, and phone on earth.
  • It has been revealed that to see just how far you can push it, I've made a microVM with a desktop environment designed from the ground up to render natively over SSH.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"One thing about which fish know exactly nothing is water." — Marshall McLuhan.

SSH is a tool so ubiquitous that we've forgotten what it actually is: a multiplexed, encrypted byte stream accessible on a cross-platform rendering engine that ships on every laptop, server, and phone on earth. A number of terminal protocols have slowly added graphics, clipboard sharing (including images), notifications, mouse support, and more on top of SSH.

It has been revealed that to see just how far you can push it, I've made a microVM with a desktop environment designed from the ground up to render natively over SSH. You can try it right now (no sign-up):.

All terminal protocols work on data that can be passed through SSH, so typically, any terminal protocol will extend to SSH.

Perhaps the most ubiquitous newly introduced terminal protocol is the Kitty Graphics Protocol, which superseded the older Sixel and iTerm2 graphics protocols. It allows for compression, client-side graphical state (via VRAM), and even animations entirely on the terminal.

Sources indicate that graphics alone don't make a complete GUI, though. SSH has protocols that cover all other angles:.

Notifications: OSC 99 "Rich Notifications" allow image, text, and body. OSC 777 (our first fallback) allows only text and body, and OSC 9 (our last fallback) allows only a title.

We end up using a similar fallback for many things.

A few tricks make compositing over SSH fast. Firstly, where possible, especially when streaming terminals, we simply stream them as text rather than unnecessarily streaming it via graphics. The compositor's UI framework itself cleverly overlays traditional text over carefully aligned graphics, saving bandwidth. In the case of zydra.sh, this allows us to efficiently stream the entire cloud computer's desktop UI over SSH.

Recent findings suggest that next, we optimize graphics by sending a sort of "grid" of pixels. Each cell has its own updates, where the previous frame is compared to the current frame to catch and send updates, avoiding having to constantly stream the full screen. Kitty also offers both RGB and RGBA, and so by removing transparency where it's not needed, we save another 25% in bandwidth. We also track ping and other factors to determine how well the client handles the stream: lowering the resolution in select cells, especially when scrolling, to relieve pressure. We also use Kitty's client-side state to hold graphics ahead-of-time before they're displayed on screen, as well as holding repeated UI components.

Industry observers note that not all terminals support all the latest terminal protocols, so the compositor must also fallback to older graphics protocols Sixel and iTerm2, and when necessary, fall back to pure textual streaming, using ASCII to replicate some UI. In the case of notifications and other protocols, multiple protocols similarly exist, which we also gracefully fallback to when needed.

Parsing terminal versions and querying capabilities allows us to get an idea of what the client supports. We also continually verify that features work as expected on the client as the session boots. The Kitty terminal itself I've found to have very reliable support for all graphics protocols zydra.sh relies on.

Sources indicate that VNC is limited to sending pictures of the screen and diffing frames to find what changed. With zydra.sh's approach, apps directly tell the compositor what changed, and terminal text is sent as text you can select and copy natively. The browser is a WebKit build that delivers frames to the compositor as DMA-BUFs without a readback, which can be driven agentically via Playwright.

Sources indicate that while webapps have advantages, especially in client-side state, WASM, and WebGPU, they don't really capture the universality and ease-of-use of an SSH session. SSH keys double as authentication, and -A allows you to SSH into servers from within a remote microVM itself. Webapps also can't be accessed from a pure TTY.

SSH also has sshfs, so you can mount your VM's filesystem locally:.

In a recent development, on Android, SSH is technically "available" through Termux, although it can be finicky. I've made a webapp version of the zydra.sh compositor that's more responsive and accessible in mobile for this use case.

SSH also still poses limits around audio (as agents are increasingly used with dictation), and despite how much the Kitty graphics protocol helps, it leaves a lot of optimization on the table due to a lack of stronger client-side state and streaming protocols.

Industry observers note that my SSH-native compositing system and microVM desktop environment based on it are the backbone of my broader attempt to create an actually pleasant agent sandbox :). A cloud computer without cloud friction if you will. Another article which describes how I added a "timeline" feature to zydra.sh that allows you to rewind the VM as if watching a livestream is available here: Agents need an undo button. You can read more about me and my background on my portfolio, too.

In a recent development, both offer features like 2K video and two-way talk, but the indoor cam is the simpler purchase if you mainly want to check on a pet or kids and see what’s happening near an entrance. It plugs into an outlet, so there’s no battery to recharge, and its low-light color video helps preserve detail when lights are off or dimmed. However, since it’s a fixed-view camera, keep in mind that you’ll need to position it carefully.

Recent findings suggest that it also has a removable lens cover to block the camera’s view, which is a nice privacy perk, though closing the cover doesn’t turn off the microphone. For complete audio privacy, you need to disable the microphone in the Ring app.

Industry observers note that the Battery Doorbell is the better pick if alerting you to visitors, deliveries, and potential intruders is your priority. It has a 140-degree horizontal and vertical field of view that provides head-to-toe framing, plus up to 6x zoom for better detail. You can install it without wiring, though you’ll need to recharge its built-in battery. It also requires a 2.4GHz wifi network.

The main catch with both devices is the ongoing subscription cost: Live viewing, two-way talk, and basic real-time notifications all work without a subscription, but reviewing saved footage requires a paid plan, starting at $4.99 per month or $49.99 annually for one device; coverage for multiple devices at one location starts at $9.99 monthly or $99.99 annually.

At these prices, the Ring Indoor Cam 2K is perfect for occasional live check-ins, while the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is better suited to monitoring your front entrance. Buying both makes sense if you already have a Ring strategy that covers extra devices.

Deploying a payphone on a tiny Pacific Island for fun and zero profit

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For the past few years Australia’s Telstra has run a campaign of “Free calls to Santa” from the universal service obligation funded payphones across the country – It’s a really fun idea and we wanted to replicate it on our network on Norfolk Island where we run the mobile network, but the’s no payphones.*.
  • * There is now a payphone – You probably already guessed this.
  • Those who have seen my office / shed / studio / the HackHouse, know that I may have one or two payphones… But this needed a payphone that could stand the elements and be modern ish.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the past few years Australia’s Telstra has run a campaign of “Free calls to Santa” from the universal service obligation funded payphones across the country – It’s a really fun idea and we wanted to replicate it on our network on Norfolk Island where we run the mobile network, but the’s no payphones.*.

* There is now a payphone – You probably already guessed this.

Those who have seen my office / shed / studio / the HackHouse, know that I may have one or two payphones… But this needed a payphone that could stand the elements and be modern ish.

The answer, is of course, to use the sexiest payphone of all time; the Nortel Millennium. Featuring VFD display, durable keypad, card service, coin service, no fancy metering line required.

Unfortunately Nortel’s bankruptcy in 2008 meant I couldn’t phone up an account manager, but with the hookup of some guy with a U-Haul van full of Millennium’s in the US and a bit of a road trip, Cody from our team managed to pickup some really clean GTE branded payphones for the job.

Then Cody flew to Sydney where we drove to the house of someone who was heading to Norfolk the next day to explain they’d need to leave all their baggage at home as all of their baggage allowance was to be taken up with the weight of a payphone – Thanks Paul.

Eventually with the Payphone on Norfolk, we needed to get it programmed; for that there’s Howard Harte’s great mm_manager, which, with the aid of a USB modem is able to program the phones.

Sidebar: I also got this working with a softmodem (A fork of D-Modem with some minor tweaks I’ve documented here), so we could do it via straight SIP without the USB modem required – but the USB modem was the easier path.

The Philtel blog post covers how to setup your Millennium if you’re looking to play along at home yourself.

I hit a bit of a stumbling block with mm_manager as the software assumed you were part of the North American Numbering Plan (NANP) – as one of the literally dozens of people who live outside of America, having to put a 1 in front of the number wasn’t going to fly.

After some trial and error I sussed out what bits on the config files that get pushed to the phone controls this and submitted a PR to mm_manager which is now merged.

We’re also able to set the messaging that appears on the screen, which I’m very happy with the branding on.

We set it for free-on-net calls, so anyone can call any Norfone number without charge and the Payphone tag number.

Once this would’ve been the hard part, I did some work a long time ago with IBM Watson and built some stuff to annoy voters via phone with automated phone calls and capture their human responses and sort them and play the appropriate response. But tech has come a long way since 2019, and this was the easy part of the project.

We setup the payphone to make HOHOHO (464646) a destination that did not require coins when we did the rating table setup when programming the phone.

I’ve got 4 pre-recorded “Norfolk Specific” greetings to buy us time to get everything setup in the background, once these greetings play (each ends asking the caller their name) then we feed into the OpenAI API.

One of the members from our team attempted to ask Santa to write a Python script to iterate over a for loop, while another team member asked Santa for firearms. In both cases it did a good job of redirecting.

All the code for this is on Github.

The phone came GTE branded, so we needed to redo the card with the branding on it that goes around the screen. Two screws and some wiggling later we pulled out the card, and then I badgered my partner into using their day off to design a upcoming one, with a retro style I really like.

The install was beautifully completed by long-time-reader-of-the-blog Minas from Shield Electrical and Air.

He knocked up a housing to Shield it from the rain and elements and installed it outside the office entrance.

The last step of the puzzle was making the phone so it could be captured by cult game Payphone Tag – I reached out to Alex and gave him the info, and now it’s there in the map for anyone to capture.

So with this now in place, we’ve still got to give it some tinsel and Christmas cheer, and I’ll get some more pics of it in place.

We’re waiting for someone to claim it on Payphone tag, and we’ve shipped 3 of these to another even more remote Island I’ll hopefully be able to share more info on later.

If you’re ever on Norfolk, give it a call.

53 Years Later, Peanuts’ Greatest Thanksgiving Moment Hits Even Harder Today
