💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that thanksgiving and Peanuts go together so well that it’s hard to imagine one without the other.
  • Apple TV’s free streaming window for the 1973 classic A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving already passed on November 14 and 15, but that hasn’t stopped viewers from firing up subscriptions or free trials to relive Charlie Brown’s chaotic backyard feast of buttered toast, popcorn, and jelly beans.
  • For all its kid-friendly charm, Peanuts was never just about the punchlines.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that thanksgiving and Peanuts go together so well that it’s hard to imagine one without the other. Snoopy’s been a fixture of the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade since 1968, and he’s back for the 100th parade this year. Add Snoopy and Woodstock popping up in Google’s 2026 Thanksgiving Doodle, and it’s safe to say the gang has late November covered.

Apple TV’s free streaming window for the 1973 classic A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving already passed on November 14 and 15, but that hasn’t stopped viewers from firing up subscriptions or free trials to relive Charlie Brown’s chaotic backyard feast of buttered toast, popcorn, and jelly beans. The special gets most of the attention every year, and for good reason. But two newspaper strips published 50 years ago deserve a little more of the spotlight.

For all its kid-friendly charm, Peanuts was never just about the punchlines. Charles M. Schulz could capture Charlie Brown’s very real holiday blues or have Linus van Pelt quietly remind everyone what Thanksgiving is about, all without losing that familiar humor. Back in November 1976, he was midway through a five-strip storyline in which a terrified Woodstock disguised himself to avoid becoming turkey-day dinner. Then Schulz delivered two unforgettable strips that put Snoopy’s quiet, fiercely loyal love for his tiny best friend front and center.

Running from November 22 to 26, 1976, right across Thanksgiving Day on November 25, Charles M. Schulz’s five-strip storyline turned one of Peanuts’ sweetest friendships into holiday gold. In the 1973 TV special A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving, Woodstock happily digs into a turkey dinner alongside Snoopy. Three years later, Schulz gave the newspaper version a much sharper twist.

Woodstock is terrified that being a bird in late November makes him a walking Thanksgiving dinner. Snoopy, the only character in the neighborhood who actually understands his chirping, doesn’t laugh off his tiny friend’s panic. He goes straight into protector mode, helping Woodstock put together a disguise with a hat and a fake mustache.

The payoff comes in the very next strip. Woodstock proudly struts past the doghouse in his hat and borrowed mustache, safe from anyone who might mistake him for the main course. Snoopy watches, pleased that his feathered sidekick can walk around in plain sight without anyone realizing he’s a bird. Then comes the line that makes the whole setup:.

Thanksgiving is a great day if you don’t get eaten.

Sources indicate that fifty years later, those two strips still land because Schulz turns the holiday upside down with such a simple joke. A cozy Thanksgiving feast becomes a survival mission from a bird’s point of view. Schulz once explained that Woodstock was his lighthearted way of showing how small and vulnerable everyone can feel in an overwhelming world. Snoopy’s response indicates everything about their friendship: he’s willing to hand over his own disguise props just to help his smallest friend feel safe. That mix of dark humor and genuine warmth is exactly what makes Peanuts feel timeless.

In a recent development, looking back at those November 1976 strips feels especially fitting now, with Peanuts having another huge year. Fresh off its 75th anniversary, the gang has been everywhere in 2026. Apple TV brought out the latest holiday special Snoopy Presents: 12 Days of Snoopy, while the brand kept popping up in major collaborations.

Starbucks kicked off fall in September with a global, Great Pumpkin-inspired merch drop featuring a barista Snoopy plush and secret-menu Frappuccinos. Timex followed in early November with four winter watches featuring a bundled-up Snoopy and Woodstock across its T80 and Weekender lines. And on December 8, Crocs is set to release a red puffer-inspired Classic Lined Clog starring Joe Cool, Snoopy’s sunglasses-wearing alter ego.

In a recent development, all that modern hype keeps Charlie Brown’s world in front of a newly introduced crowd, but Peanuts’ staying power was built on the newspaper page. Fifty years later, Schulz’s Thanksgiving punchline still lands exactly as it did the first time. In just a few panels, he could bring together dark comedy, quiet loyalty, and genuine holiday warmth. Nobody played with words quite like Schulz, and these strips are a lovely reminder of why his work still hits home.

It has been revealed that iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year.

Sources indicate that 2027 is going to be a relatively substantial iPhone release year for Apple. First, the company will be continuing the iPhone 18 lineup after it introduced a split release schedule. Then, in the fall, the company will debut a upcoming round of flagships in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. Here’s what to expect.

It has been revealed that for the first time, Apple will be introducing its base iPhone in the spring. Upgrades for the iPhone 18 aren’t quite clear, though more RAM is one of the key rumors. Thermal upgrades will likely happen as well, as well as the fresh Apple C2 modem.

It’s possible Apple will revision the design to fall more in line with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, though we don’t yet know.

This phone will of course equip the A20 chip, and it’ll probably start at the same $899 price point that iPhone 17 at the moment sits at – after it was increased from $799 in September.

In a recent development, this phone will most likely just end up being a chip bump from the A19 to A20 chip, and debut in the Spring alongside the iPhone 18. Earlier this year, reports indicated that Apple would share many components between the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, though it isn’t quite clear what that could mean for the devices.

Out of all of the spring iPhone releases, this one is the one to look forward to. After receiving a lukewarm reception with the initial iPhone Air model, Apple went back to the drawing board and decided to modify the design to fit an ultrawide camera into the device.

It has been revealed that personally, I don’t think an ultrawide camera is too vital – though many people will see one camera on the back of the phone and immediately assume it’s less premium, so it’ll probably end up being an important upgrade for the sake of sales. Plus, ultrawide photos can be fun at times.

It should also have a larger battery, reportedly as large as 3500mAh. That’s a roughly 10% improvement from the original iPhone Air. iPhone Air 2 will likely also jump from Apples C1X modem to the C2.

It has been revealed that for the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, Apple is expected to debut a fully redesigned iPhone to celebrate. It’ll reportedly be much more glassy, feature significantly slimmer bezels, a quad curved display, and ditch the flat edge design of the iPhone 12 and later.

Personally, I’m slightly skeptical that this’ll truly be a replacement to the “Pro” phone for thermal reasons, but time will tell. iPhone Duo seemingly has strong thermals while not featuring an aluminum unibody, so my concern might not be relevant. It’ll offer two, larger display sizes: 6.4-inch and 7-inch. This largely comes from the bezel reduction.

In a recent development, A novel solution for connecting to the internet on the go, the TP-Link Roam 7 travel router is now down to $83.49 from $119.99 for Black Friday, marking its lowest price to date. This isn't a full-size home router but, as the name suggests, a compact travel companion that measures roughly the size of a paperback book, with foldable antennas that let it slip easily into a bag.

More about convenience than chasing top speeds, you can use the Roam 7 as a standard router, connect it to public wifi to create a private network, or share your phone's internet through USB tethering. It also supports Ethernet input and USB modems, along with range extender and wireless client modes. That flexibility is particularly useful when you’re juggling a laptop, phone, and maybe a tablet and would prefer not to sign each one into a shaky network separately. Setup is straightforward through the TP-Link Tether app: scan a QR code, choose your connection type, and you’re online in a few minutes.

Once it’s running, the hardware covers the basics, with a 2.5 Gbps port for a wired connection like a hotel’s Ethernet jack, a 1 Gbps port for a wired device, and a USB 3.0 port for a storage drive or phone tethering. And since it draws power over USB-C (5V/3A), a basic power bank can keep it going through a long layover or a camping trip. As handy as it is on the road, though, it’s not meant to replace a full-size home router—even with its 5 GHz band and Wi-Fi 7 support—which will generally offer better coverage and more consistent speeds. Real-world performance also depends heavily on your connection and setup. USB tethering, for example, can feel slower than using your phone directly. It also leaves out features like automatic band steering, so you may end up managing networks yourself. Still, if you travel often or need a portable network hub for multiple devices, you’ll find it holds up pretty well.
